I would love for you to just talk a little bit about what that process was like and what made you decide to have a character who was such an interesting person and so not a human being.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的，所以我认为你的书中的一件事非常令人高兴，并且会让科幻小说爱好者感到高兴，那就是你显然做了很多工作来塑造这个如此陌生的角色，从人类的角度来看，成为角色的角度，并将地球和人类视为外星人，就像我们看到这个角色一样。我希望你能谈谈这个过程是什么样的，以及是什么让你决定拥有一个如此有趣的人而不是一个人的角色。

paras.en: Newitz: I mean, the thing that’s fun about this character, whose name is Gardenpath, is that they are physically very different from us. They’re a single-celled organism. They are based on a slime mold, and I did talk to a slime mold biologist to, you know, get some evidence-based, uh, descriptions of slime molds. They are very alien, but at the same time, they’re in grad school, and their grad school system, in this floating university outside of our galaxy, is quite recognizable. And so I think one of the things that is fun about it is that if you’ve at all been in academia or read about academia, you will recognize the kind of social structure.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：我的意思是，这个名叫 Gardenpath 的角色的有趣之处在于，他们在身体上与我们非常不同。它们是单细胞生物。它们是基于粘菌的，我确实和一位粘菌生物学家交谈过，你知道，得到一些基于证据的，呃，对粘菌的描述。他们非常陌生，但同时，他们正在读研究生，他们的研究生院系统，在我们银河系外的这所浮动大学中，非常容易辨认。所以我认为有趣的事情之一是，如果你曾经在学术界工作过或者读过有关学术界的文章，你就会认识到这种社会结构。

paras.en: But at the same time, we have these students who, you know, they don’t have ears or mouths as we know them, so if they wanna communicate, they’re doing it using cellular signaling, which I think I’ve always been fascinated by that mechanism, how our cells and our bodies talk to each other basically using chemicals and hormones and ions. You know, using communication that’s very, very different from ours, and so that’s what these guys are doing, and they have receptors all over the surfaces of their membranes, and they use those to communicate emotions, words, philosophies. They can reach inside of each other to communicate, which, again, is, is not totally unlike how a slime mold might communicate with another slime.
paras.zh: 但与此同时，我们有这些学生，你知道，他们没有我们所知道的耳朵或嘴巴，所以如果他们想要交流，他们会使用细胞信号传导来做到这一点，我想我一直对这种机制着迷，我们的细胞和我们的身体如何基本上使用化学物质、激素和离子相互交谈。你知道，使用与我们非常非常不同的交流方式，这就是这些人正在做的事情，他们的细胞膜表面遍布受体，他们用这些受体来交流情感、言语和哲学。它们可以到达彼此的内部进行交流，这与粘菌与另一种粘液的交流方式并不完全不同。

paras.en: One of the things, again, that I love about slime molds—because who doesn’t love slime molds?—is that in their life cycles, many of them go from being a single-celled organism to joining up with other single cells to become, sometimes they’re called slugs. They, kind of, become multicellular, sometimes to reproduce but sometimes just to walk around and find food.
paras.zh: 再说一遍，我喜欢粘菌的原因之一是，谁不喜欢粘菌呢？在它们的生命周期中，它们中的许多人从单细胞生物体转变为与其他单细胞结合在一起，有时它们被称为鼻涕虫。它们某种程度上变成了多细胞，有时是为了繁殖，有时只是为了四处走动寻找食物。

paras.en: And so my guys do that. Like, that’s their sleep cycle, is that during periods when they need to detox, basically, they merge together. And for me, it’s just really gratifying after spending many, many years writing about biology and writing about these things from a very human perspective. I just wanted to know, like, how would the cells be feeling about cellular communication, and what would it be like to be somebody who spent part of your life as an individual and part of your life merged into a larger entity?
paras.zh: 所以我的人就这么做了。就像，这就是他们的睡眠周期，在他们需要排毒的时期，基本上，他们会融合在一起。对我来说，花了很多很多年写生物学并从非常人性化的角度写这些东西之后，这真的很令人欣慰。我只是想知道，细胞对细胞通讯会有什么感觉，如果有人将你的一部分生命作为个体度过，又将你的一部分生命融入到一个更大的实体中，会是什么样子？

paras.en: Those are the kinds of questions that animate me you know I, as a journalist, of course, I strive to be as factual as possible, but then my head still fills with all these thoughts like, “What if every cell in our bodies is actually, like, an entity that’s an individual?” Or like, “What if slime molds actually have an advanced civilization?” You know, probably they don’t, but maybe they do. And so that, this is what I imagine they would be like.
paras.zh: 这些问题让我充满活力，你知道，我作为一名记者，当然，我努力尽可能真实，但我的脑海中仍然充满了所有这些想法，比如“如果我们身体中的每个细胞实际上都是一个个体的实体呢？”或者就像，“如果粘菌实际上拥有先进的文明怎么办？”你知道，他们可能不知道，但也许他们知道。所以，这就是我想象的他们会是什么样子。

paras.en: Feltman: So obviously, you talk to scientists all the time for your work, and that informed a lot of this. But I, I saw in your acknowledgments that you ran this by a few experts, and that, that got me curious. You know, how did you balance, sort of, pulling from actual biology versus letting things go and putting your own spin on them for the sake of the plot and the story?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：很明显，你一直在与科学家讨论你的工作，这给了我们很多启发。但我，我在您的致谢中看到，您是由几位专家主持的，这让我很好奇。你知道，你是如何平衡的，从实际的生物学中汲取灵感，与为了情节和故事而放任自流并加入你自己的想法？

paras.en: Newitz: That’s a really good question, and I think, for me as a writer, I like having hard limits on my imagination. I’m one of those people who hates, like, holodeck episodes on Star Trek because anything can happen. So what I tend to do is use the science as much as possible as a guardrail.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：这是一个非常好的问题，我认为，对于我作为一名作家来说，我喜欢对我的想象力有严格的限制。我是那些讨厌《星际迷航》中全息甲板的人之一，因为任何事情都有可能发生。所以我倾向于做的是尽可能多地使用科学作为护栏。

paras.en: Newitz: And so, for instance, the slime mold characters who call themselves the rational people, they live in the circumgalactic medium, which is a gas cloud that surrounds our galaxy. And I interviewed Molly Peeples, who’s a cosmologist who studies the circumgalactic medium, and we talked a lot about, like, the density of gas, the temperatures, what kinds of resources would be out there. Like, would there be water? Would there be metals? And it turns out, like, there’s planets and stars so they got whole little micro galaxies out there.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：例如，那些自称为理性人的粘菌角色，他们生活在环绕银河系的介质中，这是围绕我们银河系的气体云。我采访了莫莉·皮普尔斯（Molly Peeples），她是一位研究环银河系介质的宇宙学家，我们讨论了很多关于气体密度、温度、那里有什么资源的话题。比如，会有水吗？会有金属吗？事实证明，有行星和恒星，所以它们有完整的小微型星系。

paras.en: So to me, that provided a really great world to put my characters [in] because they actually have resources out there. But at the same time, you know, there’s a lot of stuff they don’t have: for example, intense gravity wells, like, all of the radiation that we deal with all the time inside the galactic plane.
paras.zh: 所以对我来说，这提供了一个非常伟大的世界来放置我的角色，因为他们实际上拥有资源。但与此同时，你知道，有很多东西他们没有：例如，强重力井，就像我们一直在银河平面内处理的所有辐射。

paras.en: So I guess, like, the answer to that question is: I try to be as accurate as possible, but then the thing about science is: there’s all of these areas that are, kind of, the dark matter of what we know, you know? There’s just stuff we don’t know, and so that’s where I get to come in and say, like, “Well, this is what it might be like to live out there,” or, “If a cellular slime mold were conscious, this is kind of how it would feel.” That’s all the stuff we’re not allowed to do as science journalists, and so it’s really fun to kind of break the rules and, and fill in all those gaps with my own ideas.
paras.zh: 所以我想，这个问题的答案是：我试图尽可能准确，但科学的问题是：所有这些领域都是我们所知道的暗物质，你知道吗？有些东西我们不知道，所以我就进来说，“好吧，这就是生活在那里的感觉”，或者，“如果细胞粘菌有意识，这就是它的感觉。”这些都是我们作为科学记者不允许做的事情，所以打破规则并用我自己的想法填补所有这些空白真的很有趣。

paras.en: Feltman: Definitely. What are some of your favorite aspects of, you know, this type of life and culture that you created for the book?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：当然。你为这本书创造的这种生活和文化，你最喜欢的方面是什么？

paras.en: Newitz: Well, I liked having the combination of this very alien civilization meeting Roman civilization because I feel like, as someone who writes a lot about archaeology, that I often do feel like an alien when I’m writing about a civilization that’s, like, 2,000 years old and has these recognizable elements but also so many cultural assumptions that are lost or very, very different from ours.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：嗯，我喜欢这种非常外星的文明与罗马文明的结合，因为我觉得，作为一个写了很多考古学文章的人，当我写一个大约有 2000 年历史的文明时，我经常感觉自己像个外星人，它有这些可识别的元素，但也有很多已经丢失或与我们非常非常不同的文化假设。

paras.en: Newitz: And so I liked the idea of, kind of, showing that to the reader and inviting readers to remember that human civilizations can also be so radically unlike ours today that we might as well approach them like aliens. And one thing that I speculated was that Murtis, our character who lives in Pompeii, wouldn’t really be fazed by the idea of meeting an alien because, at that time in history, you know, we hadn’t yet figured out what the stars were really. We hadn’t figured out everything that was on Earth. And so Gardenpath eventually is like, “Yeah, I’m kind of from beyond the stars, and I’m here studying.” And Murtis thinks it’s weirder that a woman is a scholar than that there’s a woman from beyond the stars visiting Pompeii, and she’s like, “Oh, well, are there Romans where you come from?” Like, because she lives in a world where Romans have kind of invaded everything.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：所以我喜欢这样的想法，向读者展示这一点，并邀请读者记住，人类文明也可能与我们今天的文明截然不同，以至于我们不妨像对待外星人一样对待它们。我推测的一件事是，穆蒂斯，我们住在庞贝的角色，不会因为遇到外星人的想法而感到困扰，因为，在历史上的那个时期，你知道，我们还没有弄清楚星星到底是什么。我们还没有弄清楚地球上的一切。所以 Gardenpath 最终会说，“是的，我来自星星之外，我在这里学习。”穆蒂斯认为，一个女人是一名学者，比一个来自星星之外的女人访问庞贝更奇怪，她说，“哦，好吧，你来自罗马人吗？”就像，因为她生活在一个罗马人几乎入侵了一切的世界。

paras.en: Newitz: And so I liked, you know, putting that stuff together and saying, like, "Well, actually, maybe in ancient Rome, you know, aliens would have seemed more ordinary than they would now."
paras.zh: 纽维茨：所以我喜欢，你知道，把这些东西放在一起然后说，“好吧，实际上，也许在古罗马，你知道，外星人看起来会比现在更普通。”

paras.en: Feltman: Right. Is it crazier than somebody who’s never heard of Rome? Like, somebody coming from the other side of the planet is as wild as somebody coming from the stars when you haven’t studied astrophysics, so....
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：对。这比从未听说过罗马的人更疯狂吗？就像，当你没有学过天体物理学时，来自地球另一边的人就像来自星星的人一样狂野，所以……

paras.en: Newitz: And when you couldn’t possibly have because nobody had been able to figure that stuff out at that level yet, you know? And of course, in Pompeii, it was such a cosmopolitan city that they would’ve had people from all over the place. People were coming from Africa, people were coming from Asia Minor, the Levant, like, Europe. So, you know, an alien is like, “Whatever.” That’s just, “Okay, you’re from beyond the stars—fine,” you know?
paras.zh: 纽维茨：当你不可能做到这一点时，因为还没有人能够在那个水平上弄清楚这些东西，你知道吗？当然，在庞贝，这是一个国际化的城市，会有来自世界各地的人们。人们来自非洲，人们来自小亚细亚、黎凡特，比如欧洲。所以，你知道，外星人就像，“随便吧。”那只是，“好吧，你来自星星之外——好吧，”你知道吗？

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. Why do you think it’s important for us to think about the idea of a consciousness that could be so different from ours and life that’s so different from what feels normal to us?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。为什么你认为思考一种与我们的意识如此不同的意识和与我们正常感觉如此不同的生活对我们来说很重要？

paras.en: Newitz: I really think it’s important to question what we think of as normal or typical, and this is an idea that science and the scientific project have always taken really seriously. I mean, the thing that’s wonderful about science is that when it’s practiced in its most pure form, it’s about asking every possible question you can about everything around you and not taking anything for granted and not assuming that what seems normal now is actually what’s normal everywhere.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：我真的认为质疑我们认为正常或典型的东西很重要，这是科学和科学项目一直非常认真对待的一个想法。我的意思是，科学的美妙之处在于，当它以最纯粹的形式实践时，它就是对周围的一切提出你能提出的所有问题，而不是认为任何事情都是理所当然的，也不假设现在看起来正常的事情实际上在任何地方都是正常的。

paras.en: And so there’s something really beautiful about getting a chance to think about: What would a very different kind of consciousness be like? You know, what would it mean to acknowledge forms of thinking, forms of cognition, that don’t fit with what we have experienced as people, uh, on Earth or as humans on Earth, really, is what I should say.
paras.zh: 因此，有机会思考是一件非常美妙的事情：一种截然不同的意识会是什么样子？你知道，承认那些与我们作为人类，呃，在地球上或作为地球上的人类所经历的不相符的思维形式、认知形式意味着什么，这就是我应该说的。

paras.en: There’s always a, kind of, sneaky undercurrent in my work because I write a lot about nonhuman consciousness, uh, in my fiction. And it’s, it’s really about trying to approach each other with more curiosity and more openness and to really approach, you know, other humans and think, “Oh, uh, even though they seem so different, maybe we have something in common, or maybe there’s just something beautiful or fascinating about how different this person is from me.”
paras.zh: 我的作品中总是有一种偷偷摸摸的暗流，因为我在小说中写了很多关于非人类意识的内容。这实际上是要尝试以更多的好奇心和更开放的态度来接近彼此，并真正接近其他人，并思考，“哦，呃，即使他们看起来如此不同，也许我们有一些共同点，或者也许这个人与我有多么不同，有一些美丽或迷人的东西。”

paras.en: Or a nonhuman animal. We’re learning more all the time about how much culture that nonhuman animals seem to have—you know, whales, elephants. I was just on a great website that has recordings of elephant communication, and there’s dozens and dozens of these vocalizations, I guess. But they’re communication, like, elephants are talking to each other, figuring out who’s gonna lead the pack today or where they’re gonna go.
paras.zh: 或者非人类动物。我们一直在更多地了解非人类动物似乎拥有多少文化——你知道，鲸鱼、大象。我刚刚访问了一个很棒的网站，里面有大象交流的录音，我猜有几十种这样的声音。但它们是在交流，就像大象互相交谈一样，弄清楚今天谁将带头，或者它们要去哪里。

paras.en: And so for me, if I can invite readers to empathize with a slime mold, I really hope they can take that back out into the real world and maybe empathize with elephants or with just human beings who seem really different.
paras.zh: 所以对我来说，如果我能邀请读者对粘菌产生共鸣，我真的希望他们能把它带回到现实世界，也许能对大象或看起来非常不同的人类产生共鸣。

paras.en: Feltman: Absolutely. I keep thinking about the aspect of the, the slime mold characters where their assigned dorm mates that they need to be glopped into a bowl with so that they can dissolve their membranes and all hang out together and how like, wow, that is, that is life, isn’t it? That people need each other, and sometimes you might not like someone, but the truth is: you gotta get glopped into the bowl with them. It’s gotta happen.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：当然。我一直在思考粘菌角色的方面，他们被指定的室友需要被放进一个碗里，这样他们就可以溶解他们的膜，然后一起出去玩，多么像，哇，那就是，这就是生活，不是吗？人们互相需要，有时你可能不喜欢某人，但事实是：你必须和他们一起进入碗里。这一定会发生。

paras.en: Newitz: You’re gonna have roommates, bad roommates, even if you live beyond the galaxy sometimes. [Laughs.] It’s a universal experience.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：你会有室友，糟糕的室友，即使你有时住在银河系之外。 [笑]这是一种普遍的体验。

paras.en: Feltman: Well, thank you so much for coming on to talk about the book. This has been great.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：嗯，非常感谢您过来谈论这本书。这太棒了。

paras.en: Newitz: Yeah. Thank you so much for having me.
paras.zh: 纽维茨：是的。非常感谢你邀请我。

paras.en: Feltman: That’s all for today’s episode. We’ll be back on Friday for a fascinating conversation about the human mind’s capacity for uncertainty—and how you can improve your own brain’s ability to cope with chaos.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这就是今天这一集的全部内容。我们将于周五回来进行一场精彩的对话，主题是人类大脑应对不确定性的能力，以及如何提高大脑应对混乱的能力。

paras.en: For Scientific American, this is Rachel Feltman. See you next time!
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》的这位人物是雷切尔·费尔特曼 (Rachel Feltman)。下次见！

articles.title: Peek into hidden worlds revealed by the 2026 Nikon Small World contest
articles.author: Allie Skalnik

paras.en: Nestled within a rebuilt inkjet printer, droplets of ink hang suspended above a page. Seen through a microscope, the droplets reveal how an inkjet printer produces crisp, uniform letters.
paras.zh: 坐落在重建的喷墨打印机内，墨滴悬挂在页面上方。通过显微镜观察，这些液滴揭示了喷墨打印机如何打印出清晰、均匀的字母。

paras.en: Ole Bielfeldt, a design student in Cologne, Germany, has been photographing the microscopic world since about 2021. His interest began as a quarantine hobby, when an old school microscope from his attic gave him a way to explore while stuck at home during the pandemic.
paras.zh: Ole Bielfeldt 是德国科隆的一名设计专业学生，大约从 2021 年开始就开始拍摄微观世界。他的兴趣始于一种隔离爱好，当时他阁楼上的一台老式显微镜为他在大流行期间困在家里提供了一种探索的方式。

paras.en: His printer image won first place in the 2026 Nikon Small World photomicrography competition. To capture the winning photo, he built a custom rig that moved the paper instead of the printer’s ink nozzles, keeping the nozzles stationary and in focus.
paras.zh: 他的打印机图像在 2026 年尼康小世界显微摄影大赛中获得第一名。为了拍摄获奖照片，他构建了一个定制装置，可以移动纸张而不是打印机的墨水喷嘴，从而保持喷嘴静止并聚焦。

paras.en: Ole Bielfeldt created this custom rig to catch impossibly fast ink droplets midflight. The contraption is only a bit larger than his head. Swipe through to see what word the printer was spitting out ink to spell.
paras.zh: Ole Bielfeldt 创造了这个定制装置，用于在飞行中捕捉难以置信的快速墨滴。这个装置只比他的头大一点。滑动鼠标即可查看打印机正在喷出墨水来拼写哪个单词。

paras.en: Bielfeldt estimates that the droplets traveled at nearly 20 meters per second — too fast for even his best slow-motion camera to resolve. To freeze their motion, Bielfeldt worked in darkness, illuminating the scene with a single brief flash. He instructed the printer to repeatedly spell out “macro,” a nod to his social media handle, macrofying.
paras.zh: Bielfeldt 估计这些水滴以每秒近 20 米的速度传播——速度太快了，即使是他最好的慢动作相机也无法分辨。为了定格他们的动作，比尔费尔特在黑暗中工作，用短暂的闪光照亮了场景。他指示打印机反复拼出“macro”，这是对他的社交媒体账号“macrofing”的致敬。

paras.en: Before this project, a printer was “like magic,” Bielfeldt says. Photographing its inner workings helped him understand how it operates.
paras.zh: 比尔费尔特说，在这个项目之前，打印机“就像魔法一样”。拍摄其内部运作方式有助于他了解其运作方式。

paras.en: Bielfeldt no longer takes the magic printers spit out for granted. “It’s so, so advanced technically, but at the same time it’s so, so common,” he says.
paras.zh: 比尔费尔特不再认为神奇打印机的出现是理所当然的。 “它在技术上非常非常先进，但同时它又非常非常普遍，”他说。

paras.en: His photograph is one of 86 images recognized in this year’s competition, whose winners were announced October 21. Here are some of our other favorites.
paras.zh: 他的照片是今年比赛中认可的 86 张照片之一，获奖者名单于 10 月 21 日公布。以下是我们最喜欢的其他一些照片。

paras.en: This pollen-dusted jumping spider offers a close look at the bristling hairs and some of its eight eyes that are easy to miss with the naked eye.
paras.zh: 这只花粉灰的跳跃蜘蛛可以近距离观察毛发和它的八只眼睛中的一些，这些眼睛很容易用肉眼看到。

paras.en: John-Oliver Dum’s fascination with spiders began as a childhood fear. Dum says he suffered a particularly painful arachnid-inflicted bite when he was young. Several years ago, when he was inspired to study the movements of a curly hair tarantula (Tliltocatl albopilosus), Dum became passionate about capturing their beauty.
paras.zh: 约翰·奥利弗·杜姆 (John-Oliver Dum) 对蜘蛛的迷恋始于童年的恐惧。杜姆说，他年轻时曾被蜘蛛咬过，特别痛苦。几年前，当 Dum 受到研究卷毛狼蛛 (Tliltocatl albopilosus) 动作的启发时，他开始热衷于捕捉它们的美丽。

paras.en: Preparations for his photographs can begin years before he submits them to a competition. His wife grows plants selected for their pollen, which Dum uses in his images.
paras.zh: 他的照片的准备工作可以在他将照片提交参加比赛之前几年开始。他的妻子种植的植物是根据花粉挑选的，杜姆在他的照片中使用了花粉。

paras.en: “The biggest challenge was finding a spider like this on the right plants, with the right pollen attached to it, at exactly the right time of year and at exactly the right moment,” he says. “You need to understand not only the spider’s behavior, but also the surrounding insect and plant life and their seasonal rhythms.”
paras.zh: “最大的挑战是在一年中正确的时间和正确的时刻，在正确的植物上找到这样的蜘蛛，并附着正确的花粉，”他说。 “你不仅需要了解蜘蛛的行为，还需要了解周围的昆虫和植物以及它们的季节节奏。”

paras.en: Dum hopes the photograph, which won second place, encourages viewers to look more closely, too. “We first have to see the beauty of this largely unknown world before we can truly understand what we may be destroying,” he says.
paras.zh: 达姆希望这张获得第二名的照片也能鼓励观众更仔细地观察。 “我们首先必须看到这个很大程度上未知的世界的美丽，然后才能真正了解我们可能正在破坏的东西，”他说。

paras.en: It’s not a leaf and it’s not a flower. This cross section of a mouse eye is crisscrossed in fractals of blood vessels and tethered by the optic nerve.
paras.zh: 它不是一片叶子，也不是一朵花。小鼠眼睛的横截面呈纵横交错的血管分形，并由视神经束缚。

paras.en: Cell biologists Sinem Karaman and Satu Paavonsalo at the University of Helsinki visualize vascular networks, like blood vessels, to study how they work within tissues. The arrangement, Paavonsalo says, could even point to mechanisms underlying how these systems stop working in obesity and diabetes.
paras.zh: 赫尔辛基大学的细胞生物学家 Sinem Karaman 和 Satu Paavonsalo 将血管网络（如血管）可视化，以研究它们在组织内的工作方式。帕冯萨洛说，这种安排甚至可能指出这些系统在肥胖和糖尿病中停止工作的潜在机制。

paras.en: Paavonsalo says the duo set out to capture a mouse eye in 3-D, different from the flattened retinas typically used in her research. After meticulous mounting which required several attempts for an arrangement she was satisfied with, Paavonsalo still didn’t know for certain the image would turn out right.
paras.zh: Paavonsalo 表示，两人开始以 3D 方式捕捉老鼠的眼睛，这与她研究中通常使用的扁平视网膜不同。经过精心安装，需要多次尝试才能获得令她满意的布置，Paavonsalo 仍然不确定图像效果是否正确。

paras.en: “I had to hope that the sample was correctly positioned and that the staining was detected throughout the sample,” Paavonsalo says, which made her excitement upon seeing the image even more pronounced. The image won 19th place in the competition.
paras.zh: Paavonsalo 说：“我不得不希望样本放置正确，并且在整个样本中检测到染色。”这让她看到图像时的兴奋更加明显。该图像在比赛中获得第 19 名。

paras.en: A water bear emerges from its shed cuticle, and oh! What’s that left behind? This egg will be protected by its mother’s discarded skin.
paras.zh: 水熊虫从脱落的角质层中钻出来，哦！那留下了什么？这个蛋将受到其母亲丢弃的皮肤的保护。

paras.en: The tardigrade (Hypsibius exemplaris) is one of nature’s toughest creatures, able to survive space by going into a state of suspended animation. This species, emerging from its former skin, is only about two-and-a-half times as wide as a strand of hair. Evolutionary developmental biologist Gonzalo Quiroga-Artigas captured the image during his studies of these tiny wonders at the University of Montpellier in France.
paras.zh: 缓步动物（Hypsibius exemplaris）是自然界最顽强的生物之一，能够通过进入假死状态在太空中生存。这个物种从原来的皮肤中长出来，宽度只有一根头发的两倍半。进化发育生物学家贡萨洛·基罗加-阿蒂加斯在法国蒙彼利埃大学研究这些微小的奇迹时捕捉到了这张照片。

paras.en: In the tardigrade life cycle, “egg laying is closely synchronized with molting,” says Quiroga-Artigas. Tardigrades can lay up to about a dozen eggs at once, and the moment one sheds its old cuticle happens quickly enough that it’s easy to miss.
paras.zh: Quiroga-Artigas 说，在缓步动物的生命周期中，“产卵与蜕皮密切同步”。缓步动物一次最多可以产下十几个卵，而其中一个卵脱落旧角质层的那一刻发生得足够快，很容易被忽视。

paras.en: Snapping this image demanded painstaking mounting and imaging of many specimens. Quiroga-Artigas chose this particular one, which won 12th, because “the egg looks almost like a precious gem being left behind by its mother.”
paras.zh: 拍摄这张照片需要对许多标本进行艰苦的安装和成像。 Quiroga-Artigas 选择了这个特别的鸡蛋，获得第 12 名，因为“这颗鸡蛋看起来几乎就像是母亲留下的珍贵宝石。”

paras.en: This slime mold (Hemitrichia sp.) was found in the heart of Brooklyn, N.Y., sprouting from a decaying log in Prospect Park. The image features the mold’s gelatinous fruiting bodies, which release spores as part of reproduction. To bring the delicate structures into sharp detail, Eric Epstein stacked 240 images.
paras.zh: 这种粘菌（Hemitrichia sp.）是在纽约布鲁克林市中心发现的，它是从展望公园的一根腐烂的木头上发芽的。该图像展示了霉菌的凝胶状子实体，其释放孢子作为繁殖的一部分。为了将精致的结构呈现为清晰的细节，Eric Epstein 堆叠了 240 张图像。

paras.en: First, Epstein searched local parks for slime molds to photograph, carefully cutting pieces of waterlogged wood free without disturbing his subjects. “In this liquidy state, any touch would demolish” the fruiting bodies, he says.
paras.zh: 首先，爱泼斯坦在当地公园寻找粘菌进行拍摄，小心翼翼地切掉浸水的木头，而不打扰他的拍摄对象。 “在这种液体状态下，任何触摸都会破坏”子实体，他说。

paras.en: One species of slime mold closely mirrors the cosmic web of gas and dark matter connecting galaxies, which helps scientists to more accurately map the cosmos. Another species has fascinated researchers for its ability to pack a store of bacteria to feed the next generation, when it’s near death.
paras.zh: 一种粘菌密切地反映了连接星系的气体和暗物质的宇宙网络，这有助于科学家更准确地绘制宇宙图。另一种物种令研究人员着迷，因为它能够在下一代濒临死亡时储存大量细菌来喂养下一代。

paras.en: Epstein hopes the photograph hints “at [a] vast array of activity beyond our unaided perception.” The image won sixth place in the competition.
paras.zh: 爱泼斯坦希望这张照片暗示“一系列超出我们肉眼感知的活动”。该图像在比赛中获得了第六名。

paras.en: This cell could have become anything in the body. Through some scientific nudging, it burst into a brilliant neuron.
paras.zh: 这个细胞可以变成体内的任何东西。经过一些科学的推动，它突然变成了一个聪明的神经元。

paras.en: Clusters of nuclei, looking like flashpoints in an intricate web, were captured by undergraduate student Faith Fernandes and structural cell biologist James Glover at the University of California, Berkeley.
paras.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校的本科生 Faith Fernandes 和结构细胞生物学家 James Glover 捕捉到了看起来像错综复杂的网络中的闪点的细胞核簇。

paras.en: The image commemorates the team’s first attempt at crafting neurons from a particular kind of stem cell. “I was so instantly enamored with this piece that I made it my computer wallpaper as soon as it was taken,” Fernandes says.
paras.zh: 该图像是为了纪念该团队首次尝试从特定类型的干细胞中制造神经元。 “我立刻就被这幅作品迷住了，拍完后我就把它作为我的电脑壁纸，”费尔南德斯说。

paras.en: The eruption of color depicts human induced pluripotent stem cells, which can become any type of cell in the body, that have developed into neurons. The neurotubules, which contribute to the structure of and transportation of intracellular molecules, appear blue. Orange indicates where the DNA is located.
paras.zh: 颜色的爆发描绘了人类诱导的多能干细胞，它可以成为体内任何类型的细胞，并发育成神经元。有助于细胞内分子的结构和运输的神经管呈蓝色。橙色表示 DNA 所在的位置。

paras.en: The stem cells are created by reprogramming adult cells to a stage before the cell was locked into a path to become a specific type of cell. They are studied for their many potential applications in regenerative medicine.
paras.zh: 干细胞是通过将成体细胞重新编程到细胞被锁定成为特定类型细胞的路径之前的阶段而产生的。人们对它们在再生医学中的许多潜在应用进行了研究。

paras.en: Fernandes says she hopes that studying these cells will illuminate ways to address neurodegeneration in diseases such as Parkinson’s disease. Already, researchers have used these cells to regrow eye tissue, address premature aging in mouse studies and grow organs. The shot won an Image of Distinction title in the competition.
paras.zh: 费尔南德斯说，她希望研究这些细胞能够阐明解决帕金森病等疾病中神经退行性疾病的方法。研究人员已经利用这些细胞来再生眼组织、解决小鼠研究中的过早衰老问题以及培育器官。该镜头在比赛中获得了“杰出形象”称号。

articles.title: A lifesaving medication is not behind the drop in U.S. overdose deaths
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: Drug overdose deaths unexpectedly took a nosedive in the United States a few years ago. But it doesn’t appear to be due to more people being revived than before.
paras.zh: 几年前，美国吸毒过量死亡人数出人意料地大幅下降。但这似乎并不是因为复活的人比以前更多。

paras.en: At the peak in mid-2023, there were around 111,000 drug overdose deaths per year in the United States. By the end of 2025, the number had fallen to under 71,000 per year, and researchers are still piecing together why. One theory: The wider availability of naloxone, a medication that reverses opioid overdoses, made it possible to revive more people than before.
paras.zh: 在 2023 年中期的高峰期，美国每年约有 111,000 人因药物过量死亡。到 2025 年底，这一数字已降至每年 71,000 人以下，研究人员仍在拼凑原因。一种理论是：纳洛酮（一种逆转阿片类药物过量的药物）的广泛使用使得比以前更多的人得以复活。

paras.en: But a study of U.S. emergency medical services agencies found that emergency medical responses for nonfatal overdoses dropped along with deaths, and the use of naloxone also declined. That suggests that fewer overdoses overall occurred, not that naloxone stopped deaths more often, researchers report October 21 in the Journal of the American Medical Association.
paras.zh: 但对美国紧急医疗服务机构的一项研究发现，对非致命性用药过量的紧急医疗反应随着死亡人数的减少而下降，纳洛酮的使用也有所下降。研究人员 10 月 21 日在《美国医学会杂志》上报告称，这表明总体上服用过量的情况较少，而不是纳洛酮更频繁地阻止了死亡。

paras.en: “Naloxone still saves lives every day,” says Michael Barnett, a health services researcher at Brown University School of Public Health in Providence, R.I. “But it doesn’t look like the reason for the sudden turn” in overdose deaths.
paras.zh: 罗得岛州普罗维登斯布朗大学公共卫生学院的卫生服务研究员迈克尔·巴尼特说：“纳洛酮仍然每天都在拯救生命，但它看起来不像是过量死亡突然转变的原因”。

paras.en: State policies, community distribution programs and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s approval of the nasal spray version of naloxone as an over-the counter drug have expanded access.
paras.zh: 国家政策、社区分配计划以及美国食品和药物管理局批准鼻喷雾剂纳洛酮作为非处方药扩大了使用范围。

paras.en: Barnett and colleagues analyzed nearly 186 million emergency medical service activations — an ambulance or other EMS response after a 911 call — nationwide that occurred from May 2020 through December 2025. Of 2.5 million responses for nonfatal drug overdoses, 40.5 percent involved opioids.
paras.zh: Barnett 及其同事分析了 2020 年 5 月至 2025 年 12 月期间全国范围内发生的近 1.86 亿次紧急医疗服务启动（即接到 911 电话后救护车或其他 EMS 响应）。在 250 万次非致命药物过量响应中，40.5% 涉及阿片类药物。

paras.en: From May of 2023 onward, EMS activations for nonfatal opioid overdoses fell on average by about 6,000, or around 33 percent, below what was expected. Total administrations of naloxone dropped as well, by around 4,700 on average, or 21 percent below what was expected. The study suggests that naloxone was not used more often than before by bystanders prior to the EMS response, but did not include data on cases when a bystander provided naloxone and no one called 911.
paras.zh: 从 2023 年 5 月起，非致命阿片类药物过量的 EMS 激活平均下降约 6,000 例，即约 33%，低于预期。纳洛酮的给药总数也有所下降，平均减少约 4,700 次，比预期低 21%。该研究表明，在 EMS 响应之前，旁观者使用纳洛酮的频率并不比以前更高，但不包括旁观者提供纳洛酮且无人拨打 911 的情况的数据。

paras.en: Additional possibilities to explain the steep drop in overdose deaths — which followed a three-decade increase — include changes to the illicit opioid supply or with the population of people at risk for overdoses. “My own read is that a disruption in the fentanyl supply best explains how sudden and widespread the turn was,” Barnett says. “Underneath it, the population at risk has probably been shrinking for years.”
paras.zh: 解释服药过量死亡人数在过去三个十年增加之后急剧下降的其他可能性包括非法阿片类药物供应的变化或面临服药过量风险的人口数量。 “我自己的解读是，芬太尼供应的中断最能解释这种转变的突然性和广泛性，”巴尼特说。 “在其之下，面临风险的人口多年来可能一直在减少。”

paras.en: But “a supply-driven decline can reverse,” Barnett says, noting that the decline in overdose deaths slowed in 2025. Traffickers can adapt “by finding new chemical sources or turning to more potent synthetic opioids.”
paras.zh: 但巴尼特表示，“供应驱动的下降可能会逆转”，并指出 2025 年用药过量死亡人数的下降速度会放缓。贩运者可以“通过寻找新的化学来源或转向更有效的合成阿片类药物”来适应。

articles.title: AI could turn scientific papers into research assistants
articles.author: Kathryn Hulick

paras.en: Scientific papers may be getting a 21st century update.
paras.zh: 科学论文可能会在 21 世纪得到更新。

paras.en: A system called Paper2Agent lets scientists do more than read a new scientific study. When a paper comes with code, methods and data, the system packages these into a tool set that an AI assistant can use to work with new data, researchers report September 16 in Nature.
paras.zh: 一个名为 Paper2Agent 的系统可以让科学家做的不仅仅是阅读新的科学研究。研究人员于 9 月 16 日在《自然》杂志上报道，当一篇论文附带代码、方法和数据时，系统会将它们打包到一个工具集中，人工智能助手可以使用该工具集来处理新数据。

paras.en: The system is essentially “a virtual author of the paper,” available around the clock, says James Zou, a computer scientist at Stanford University.
paras.zh: 斯坦福大学计算机科学家 James Zou 表示，该系统本质上是“论文的虚拟作者”，全天候可用。

paras.en: In tests, Zou and colleagues tried to convert 100 computational biology papers into working tool sets and succeeded with 74. The others had obstacles such as missing code or data, or software that wouldn’t run. With the papers that were converted, the Paper2Agent tool set could run analyses of the published work and answer questions about the results. It did so more accurately and also more than twice as fast as the same agent working from the original papers and accompanying code.
paras.zh: 在测试中，Zou 和同事尝试将 100 篇计算生物学论文转换为工作工具集，其中 74 篇成功。其他论文则遇到了一些障碍，例如缺少代码或数据，或者软件无法运行。通过转换后的论文，Paper2Agent 工具集可以对已发表的论文进行分析并回答有关结果的问题。与使用原始论文和随附代码进行工作的同一代理相比，它的准确性更高，速度也快两倍多。

paras.en: Making another scientist’s code usable can take substantial work, says Peter Clark, a senior research director at the Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Seattle who was not involved in developing Paper2Agent. Researchers already share code on platforms such as GitHub. But Clark says he often has to “grub around” for half a day to figure out how to get it running.
paras.zh: 西雅图艾伦人工智能研究所的高级研究主任彼得·克拉克（Peter Clark）没有参与 Paper2Agent 的开发，他表示，让另一位科学家的代码可用可能需要大量工作。研究人员已经在 GitHub 等平台上共享代码。但克拉克表示，他经常需要“摸索”半天才能弄清楚如何让它运行。

paras.en: A general-purpose AI assistant such as Claude can help, he says, but it typically generates new code on the fly. Paper2Agent instead packages code associated with a paper into reusable tools, tests them against reference outputs and writes step-by-step instructions guiding an AI assistant on which tools to use and in what order. This streamlines and standardizes the process of using AI to interact with scientific research, Clark says. It’s “an exciting step” toward papers that actively help scientists.
paras.zh: 他说，像克劳德这样的通用人工智能助手可以提供帮助，但它通常会动态生成新代码。 Paper2Agent 相反，将与论文相关的代码打包到可重用的工具中，根据参考输出对其进行测试，并编写分步指令，指导人工智能助手使用哪些工具以及按什么顺序使用。克拉克说，这简化并标准化了使用人工智能与科学研究互动的过程。这是朝着积极帮助科学家的论文迈出的“令人兴奋的一步”。

paras.en: To Zou, transforming scientific papers into agents seem like a natural next step for transmitting knowledge. We’ve already moved from stone tablets and papyrus to paper and then to digital formats, he says, and now it’s time to move from passive to active formats for human knowledge. A paper-agent can help one human scientist quickly use another’s code and methods. The tool can also search for paper-agents about similar topics with the aim of alerting their human authors about potential collaborations.
paras.zh: 对于邹来说，将科学论文转化为媒介似乎是传播知识的自然下一步。他说，我们已经从石碑和纸莎草纸转向纸张，然后转向数字格式，现在是人类知识从被动格式转向主动格式的时候了。论文代理可以帮助一位人类科学家快速使用另一位科学家的代码和方法。该工具还可以搜索类似主题的论文代理，目的是提醒人类作者潜在的合作。

paras.en: Zou says his team has already created “over 100 different paper-agents” from their own work and that these have already helped him find other scientists to collaborate with.
paras.zh: Zou 表示，他的团队已经根据自己的工作创建了“100 多种不同的纸质代理”，这些已经帮助他找到了其他科学家进行合作。

paras.en: Clark notes that Paper2Agent specializes in helping scientists reuse methods and code, and not in answering general questions, like a true virtual author should be able to do. Also, he worries about what could happen if millions of low-quality papers get turned into agents capable of pestering scientists. That could make things “worse rather than better,” he says, recalling the days of Clippy, the much-maligned Microsoft Office assistant. But he’d love for a “non-annoying agent” to pop up and tell him about work that he should be paying attention to.
paras.zh: Clark 指出，Paper2Agent 专门帮助科学家重用方法和代码，而不是像真正的虚拟作者那样回答一般问题。此外，他还担心，如果数以百万计的低质量论文变成了能够困扰科学家的媒介，会发生什么。他回忆起饱受诟病的 Microsoft Office 助手 Clippy 的日子时说，这可能会让事情“变得更糟而不是更好”。但他希望有一个“不烦人的代理人”突然出现并告诉他他应该关注的工作。

paras.en: For more open-ended questions about a paper, Clark says he would still want to talk to the people who did the research. “The reason I would write to a corresponding author is for precisely the things they didn’t put in the paper.”
paras.zh: 对于有关论文的更多开放式问题，克拉克表示他仍然想与进行这项研究的人交谈。 “我之所以给通讯作者写信，正是因为他们没有在论文中提到的内容。”

articles.title: Scientists Found a Bizarre Pattern in Over 1,000 Cases of Alleged Human Reincarnation
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: Over 30 percent of Americans believe in the concept of reincarnation, the notion that people who die will be reborn again in this world.
paras.zh: 超过30%的美国人相信轮回的概念，即死去的人会在这个世界上重生。

paras.en: While there's no firm scientific evidence suggesting that it actually happens – nor of what happens to our consciousness after we die – the study of reincarnation, and our beliefs about it, is still a serious focus of scientific research.
paras.zh: 虽然没有确凿的科学证据表明它确实发生过——也没有表明我们死后我们的意识会发生什么——但对转世的研究以及我们对转世的信念仍然是科学研究的一个重点焦点。

paras.en: For decades, in fact, researchers have investigated what's known as Cases of the Reincarnation Type (CORT) – instances in which people, predominantly children, appear to report memories and details of somebody else's life.
paras.zh: 事实上，几十年来，研究人员一直在调查所谓的转世类型案例（CORT）——在这种情况下，人们（主要是儿童）似乎会报告别人生活的记忆和细节。

paras.en: Since the 1960s, researchers at the University of Virginia's Division of Perceptual Studies have collected information on thousands of these strange cases, representing the largest dataset of its kind.
paras.zh: 自 20 世纪 60 年代以来，弗吉尼亚大学感知研究部的研究人员收集了数千个此类奇怪案例的信息，这是同类数据中最大的数据集。

paras.en: Now, a new analysis of that trove of data has revealed a striking pattern in these mysterious episodes.
paras.zh: 现在，对大量数据的新分析揭示了这些神秘事件中的惊人模式。

paras.en: In cases where the identified deceased individual died suddenly or unexpectedly, the "intermission time" – the amount of time between their death and the birth of the child recalling their life – was significantly shorter than in cases where the death wasn't unexpected.
paras.zh: 在已确定的死者突然或意外死亡的情况下，“中场休息时间”——他们死亡和孩子出生之间的时间可以回忆起他们的生活——比非意外死亡的情况要短得多。

paras.en: The findings, reported in Psychology of Consciousness: Theory, Research, and Practice, can't really be explained, researchers say.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，《意识心理学：理论、研究与实践》中报道的这一发现无法真正得到解释。

paras.en: "This is the largest systematic study to date of temporal patterns in reported past-life memories," says lead author and cognitive neuroscience researcher Saeedeh Sadeghi from the University of Virginia.
paras.zh: “这是迄今为止最大的关于前世记忆时间模式的系统研究，”弗吉尼亚大学的主要作者、认知神经科学研究人员 Saeedeh Sadeghi 说。

paras.en: "Individual cases can leave room for different interpretations, but patterns across many cases are much harder to explain as exaggeration, fantasy or fabrication."
paras.zh: “个别案件可以留下不同解释的空间，但许多案件的模式很难用夸张、幻想或捏造来解释。”

paras.en: In their study, researchers analyzed every case in the Division of Perceptual Studies' CORT archive where investigators had been able to identify a named deceased individual (aka "Past Person") whose life and biographical details corresponded to statements collected from children who supposedly remembered things about the Past Person's life.
paras.zh: 在他们的研究中，研究人员分析了感知研究部门 CORT 档案中的每个案例，调查人员能够识别出一个已命名的已故个体（又名“过去的人”），其生活和传记细节与从据称记得有关过去的人生活的孩子那里收集的陈述相对应。

paras.en: "Trained investigators conducted comprehensive interviews with multiple informants for each case, such as the child, parents, close relatives, and sometimes family friends and neighbors," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“训练有素的调查人员对每个案件的多名线人进行了全面采访，例如孩子、父母、近亲，有时还有家庭朋友和邻居。”

paras.en: "Investigators systematically evaluated evidence from multiple sources … to systematically explore conventional explanations of the child's statements as well as the possibility of anomalous ones."
paras.zh: “调查人员系统地评估了来自多个来源的证据……系统地探索对儿童陈述的常规解释以及异常陈述的可能性。”

paras.en: The researchers analyzed 1,678 cases involving an ostensibly identified Past Person, finding that the median intermission time was 16 months among the 1,319 cases with available timing data.
paras.zh: 研究人员分析了 1,678 个涉及表面上已识别的“过去的人”的案例，发现在具有可用时间数据的 1,319 个案例中，中位间歇时间为 16 个月。

paras.en: But the more unexpected the death was – whether due to an accident, violence, or a sudden medical crisis – the shorter the intermission time tended to be.
paras.zh: 但死亡越出乎意料——无论是由于事故、暴力还是突发的医疗危机——中场休息时间往往就越短。

paras.en: In cases where the death was completely unexpected, the median intermission time was only 12 months, reflecting a roughly 43 percent reduction from the most anticipated deaths (21 months).
paras.zh: 在死亡完全出乎意料的情况下，中位间隔时间仅为 12 个月，比最预期的死亡人数（21 个月）减少了约 43%。

paras.en: What's more, the effect remained when the researchers accounted for a range of other factors, including the quality of the verified information, the level of accuracy of children's statements, prior acquaintance between families, social status, and religious beliefs.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，当研究人员考虑到一系列其他因素时，包括经过验证的信息的质量、儿童陈述的准确性水平、家庭之间的先前认识、社会地位和宗教信仰，这种影响仍然存在。

paras.en: "The effect remained even after we accounted for several cultural and psychological factors, and it was actually stronger in families whose religions did not support reincarnation," says social psychologist Philip Cozzolino of the University of Virginia.
paras.zh: 弗吉尼亚大学的社会心理学家菲利普·科佐利诺（Philip Cozzolino）表示：“即使我们考虑了一些文化和心理因素，这种影响仍然存在，而且在宗教不支持转世的家庭中，这种影响实际上更强烈。”

paras.en: "These results do not support the idea that social beliefs are driving this pattern."
paras.zh: “这些结果并不支持社会信仰推动这种模式的观点。”

paras.en: Of course, none of this should be taken as evidence that reincarnation necessarily occurred in these instances, and the researchers acknowledge that the strength of the observed association was modest, with death unexpectedness accounting for only about 2–3 percent of the variance in intermission time.
paras.zh: 当然，所有这些都不应被视为在这些情况下必然发生转世的证据，研究人员承认，观察到的关联强度不大，意外死亡仅占中场休息时间方差的 2-3% 左右。

paras.en: Still, the fact that the pattern can be seen in the data is hard to explain, the researchers say, noting it's not something that can be accounted for by existing psychosocial mechanisms.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，研究人员表示，在数据中看到这种模式的事实很难解释，并指出这不能用现有的心理社会机制来解释。

paras.en: "The noteworthy finding is not that death circumstances strongly predict intermission time, but that they predict it at all – despite the absence of an established conventional mechanism linking the two," the team explains.
paras.zh: 研究小组解释说：“值得注意的发现并不是死亡情况强烈预测了中场休息时间，而是他们确实预测了这一点——尽管缺乏将两者联系起来的既定传统机制。”

paras.en: While that's the case, the researchers observe that many cultural and religious traditions from around the world are imbued with concepts that treat unexpected deaths as leaving unfinished business on the part of the deceased.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，研究人员观察到，世界各地的许多文化和宗教传统都充满了这样的观念，即将意外死亡视为死者未完成的事情。

paras.en: "Across a number of reincarnation-oriented traditions – including Hindu, Buddhist, and Indigenous North American frameworks – abrupt or premature death may leave unresolved intentions, attachments, or obligations, creating a stronger impetus toward rebirth," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“在许多以转世为导向的传统中，包括印度教、佛教和北美土著框架，突然或过早的死亡可能会留下未解决的意图、依恋或义务，从而为重生创造更强大的动力。”

paras.en: Even outside the scope of reincarnation belief, many cultures view people who die violently or suddenly as remaining more closely connected to the living world.
paras.zh: 即使在转世信仰的范围之外，许多文化也认为暴力或突然死亡的人与生活世界的联系更加紧密。

paras.en: We don't know yet whether these kinds of cultural beliefs somehow influence the patterns observed in reported past-life memories, but future research into this strange phenomenon might provide some answers.
paras.zh: 我们还不知道这些文化信仰是否会以某种方式影响在报告的前世记忆中观察到的模式，但未来对这种奇怪现象的研究可能会提供一些答案。

paras.en: "Is this evidence of anything metaphysical? The data are observational and we're careful to stay agnostic about mechanism," Sadeghi says.
paras.zh: “这是任何形而上学的证据吗？数据是观察性的，我们小心地保持对机制的不可知论，”萨德吉说。

paras.en: "What I can say is that the pattern is real in the data, and not readily explained by cultural and psychological factors we examined – which, to me, is a reason to keep looking, not to look away."
paras.zh: “我能说的是，这种模式在数据中是真实的，并且很难用我们研究的文化和心理因素来解释——对我来说，这是一个继续寻找而不是移开目光的理由。”

paras.en: The findings are reported in Psychology of Consciousness: Theory, Research, and Practice.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《意识心理学：理论、研究和实践》中。

articles.title: Physicists Trapped a Particle of Antimatter And Kept It Caged For Months
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: The Universe, according to theory at least, should not exist.
paras.zh: 至少根据理论，宇宙不应该存在。

paras.en: Every particle in the Universe has a corresponding antimatter counterpart. Should ever a pair of such particles meet, they would immediately cancel each other out – annihilated in a tiny puff of energy.
paras.zh: 宇宙中的每个粒子都有一个相应的反物质对应物。一旦一对这样的粒子相遇，它们就会立即相互抵消——湮灭在一小股能量中。

paras.en: Theoretically, the birth of the Universe should have produced equal quantities of particles and antiparticles.
paras.zh: 从理论上讲，宇宙的诞生应该产生等量的粒子和反粒子。

paras.en: Why the current Universe is so heavily skewed in particles' favor is an enduring mystery – one whose solution remains all the harder to find because of antiparticles' tendency to go and collide with particles.
paras.zh: 为什么当前的宇宙如此严重地偏向粒子，这是一个持久的谜——由于反粒子倾向于与粒子碰撞，其解决方案仍然更难找到。

paras.en: But an extraordinary effort may have finally tamed one of the biggest tricksters of the antiparticle milieu – the positron, the antimatter counterpart to the ubiquitous electron.
paras.zh: 但一项非凡的努力可能最终驯服了反粒子环境中最大的骗子之一——正电子，它是无处不在的电子的反物质对应物。

paras.en: In a cryogenic, superconducting vacuum trap, physicists at Northwestern University in the US successfully kept a single positron for months – a breakthrough that, they say, paves the way to the most rigorous probes yet of particle physics.
paras.zh: 在低温超导真空陷阱中，美国西北大学的物理学家成功地将单个正电子保留了几个月——他们说，这一突破为迄今为止最严格的粒子物理学探测铺平了道路。

paras.en: "The biggest challenge is to persuade a positron that is ejected from a nucleus in a radioactive decay with a very high energy to slow down enough that we can capture it into our particle trap," Northwestern physicist Gerald Gabrielse, the paper's senior author, told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 该论文的资深作者、西北大学物理学家杰拉尔德·加布里埃尔斯 (Gerald Gabrielse) 告诉《ScienceAlert》：“最大的挑战是说服在放射性衰变中从原子核中喷射出的具有极高能量的正电子减速到足以让我们能够将其捕获到粒子陷阱中。”

paras.en: The Universe naturally makes positrons in a variety of ways – cosmic explosions, energetic interactions between particles, and radioactive decay, when an unstable nucleus spits out a positively charged particle otherwise identical to a negatively charged electron.
paras.zh: 宇宙自然地以多种方式产生正电子——宇宙爆炸、粒子之间的能量相互作用以及放射性衰变，即不稳定的原子核释放出带正电的粒子，否则与带负电的电子相同。

paras.en: But the Universe is not kind to positrons. All it has to do to be wiped from existence is encounter a single electron – and electrons are absolutely everywhere.
paras.zh: 但宇宙对正电子并不友善。只要遇到一个电子，它就会从存在中消失——而电子绝对无处不在。

paras.en: Physicists have been able to observe positrons since the 1930s, but to study one for any length of time would involve completely isolating it from encountering any other matter.
paras.zh: 自 20 世纪 30 年代以来，物理学家就能够观测正电子，但要研究一个正电子，无论时间长短，都需要将其与任何其他物质完全隔离。

paras.en: That's tricky, but not impossible. An electromagnetic trap can keep a single particle hovering in place in a vacuum so that it doesn't accidentally touch another particle.
paras.zh: 这很棘手，但并非不可能。电磁陷阱可以使单个粒子在真空中悬浮在适当的位置，这样它就不会意外接触到另一个粒子。

paras.en: The problem lies in bringing a particle ejected during the energetic process of radioactive decay to a standstill.
paras.zh: 问题在于如何使放射性衰变的能量过程中喷射出的粒子停止。

paras.en: "Most of the positrons that emerge from the source are not successfully slowed and captured," Gabrielse explained. "They end up 'annihilating' with an electron in our apparatus."
paras.zh: 加布里埃尔斯解释说：“大多数从源中出现的正电子都没有被成功减速和捕获。” “它们最终会用我们装置中的电子‘湮灭’。”

paras.en: The team's solution, spearheaded by Northwestern physicist Tom Myers, had to address both challenges: putting the brakes on the positron, and confining it without bringing it into contact with an electron.
paras.zh: 由西北大学物理学家汤姆·迈尔斯牵头的团队的解决方案必须解决这两个挑战：对正电子施加制动，并限制它而不使其与电子接触。

paras.en: The researchers used a radioactive isotope of sodium as their positron factory, which spits out the antiparticles with an energy of up to around 546 kiloelectronvolts – about 88 percent of the speed of light.
paras.zh: 研究人员使用钠的放射性同位素作为正电子工厂，释放出能量高达约 546 千电子伏的反粒子，约为光速的 88%。

paras.en: So how do you put the brakes on a relativistic positron?
paras.zh: 那么如何抑制相对论性正电子呢？

paras.en: Well, in this case, the answer is doing the very thing the researchers were ultimately trying to avoid – making it pass through matter. A single crystal of tungsten, to be precise.
paras.zh: 好吧，在这种情况下，答案就是做研究人员最终试图避免的事情——让它穿过物质。准确地说，是钨的单晶。

paras.en: The experimental apparatus had three main components: the sodium source, the crystal, and the trap.
paras.zh: 实验装置由三个主要部分组成：钠源、晶体和陷阱。

paras.en: First, some of the positrons emitted by the sodium source flew into the tungsten crystal, where their positive electric charge interacted with the negatively charged electrons in the material. Those interactions can excite or ionize atoms, transferring some of the positron's kinetic energy to the crystal.
paras.zh: 首先，钠源发射的一些正电子飞入钨晶体，它们的正电荷与材料中带负电的电子相互作用。这些相互作用可以激发或电离原子，将部分正电子的动能转移到晶体。

paras.en: Most of the positrons don't make it. They smack into electrons, and both are wiped out. But a scant few survive, emerging from the tungsten's surface significantly slowed, hitched to – but not touching – an electron. This is positronium.
paras.zh: 大多数正电子都无法成功。它们撞上电子，然后两者都被消灭了。但只有少数能幸存下来，从钨表面出现的速度明显减慢，附着在电子上，但没有接触到电子。这是正电子素。

paras.en: In this particular form of positronium, the electron and positron occupy a highly excited quantum state that keeps them relatively far apart, delaying their inevitable annihilation just long enough to transport the positron where it needs to go – straight into the prepared trap.
paras.zh: 在这种特殊形式的正电子中，电子和正电子占据高度激发的量子态，使它们保持相对较远的距离，将它们不可避免的湮灭延迟了足够长的时间，以便将正电子传输到它需要去的地方——直接进入准备好的陷阱。

paras.en: That trap is also ingenious. A tiny opening, just 640 micrometers wide, allows the positronium to enter, where an electric field strips away the electron, leaving the positron behind.
paras.zh: 这个陷阱也很巧妙。正电子素可以进入一个仅 640 微米宽的微小开口，电场会剥离电子，留下正电子。

paras.en: The device, called a Penning trap, uses a combination of electric and magnetic fields to confine the charged particle without allowing it to touch the walls.
paras.zh: 该装置称为潘宁陷阱，利用电场和磁场的组合来限制带电粒子，不允许其接触墙壁。

paras.en: Kept in an extraordinarily good vacuum trap cooled to just 300 millikelvins – a fraction of a degree above absolute zero – the positron can remain isolated from the outside world.
paras.zh: 正电子被保存在一个冷却至仅 300 毫开尔文（比绝对零高几分之一度）的非常好的真空阱中，可以保持与外界的隔离。

paras.en: For the researchers, it's a tense experience.
paras.zh: 对于研究人员来说，这是一次紧张的经历。

paras.en: "We turn on our detector and wait," Gabrielse said.
paras.zh: “我们打开探测器并等待，”加布里埃尔斯说。

paras.en: "Eventually we see the electrical signal from a captured positron. We then pull the radioactive source away from the trap to keep any additional positron from loading."
paras.zh: “最终我们看到来自捕获的正电子的电信号。然后我们将放射源从陷阱中拉开，以防止加载任何额外的正电子。”

paras.en: The researchers could keep their captive positron for months. But merely preventing it from annihilating was only the beginning.
paras.zh: 研究人员可以将捕获的正电子保存数月。但仅仅阻止它毁灭只是一个开始。

paras.en: They also needed to control its motion with extraordinary precision.
paras.zh: 他们还需要以非凡的精度控制其运动。

paras.en: Within the trap's powerful magnetic field, the positron moves in tiny circles – a motion called cyclotron motion. By cooling it to its lowest quantum energy state, the researchers could then use carefully tuned microwaves to nudge it between discrete energy levels, one quantum at a time.
paras.zh: 在陷阱的强大磁场内，正电子以微小的圆圈运动——这种运动称为回旋运动。通过将其冷却到最低的量子能态，研究人员可以使用精心调谐的微波将其在离散的能级之间微移，一次一个量子。

paras.en: And crucially, they could detect those changes, along with flips in the positron's spin, without disturbing the quantum states being measured.
paras.zh: 至关重要的是，他们可以检测这些变化以及正电子自旋的翻转，而不会干扰正在测量的量子态。

paras.en: "I and my research group have been pursuing a one-positron quantum cyclotron for many years, so observing a positron making one-quantum energy jumps was extremely satisfying," Gabrielse said.
paras.zh: 加布里埃尔斯说：“我和我的研究小组多年来一直在追求单正电子量子回旋加速器，因此观察正电子进行单量子能量跃迁是非常令人满意的。”

paras.en: "It was also great to see Tom's PhD thesis work culminating in a great success. He had worked very hard."
paras.zh: “看到汤姆的博士论文取得巨大成功也很高兴。他工作非常努力。”

paras.en: So why would anyone want to trap and measure a positron in the first place?
paras.zh: 那么为什么有人想要捕获并测量正电子呢？

paras.en: Actually, there are a lot of very good reasons – and somewhere near the top of the list is a fundamental principle of physics called CPT symmetry.
paras.zh: 事实上，有很多很好的理由——其中靠近列表顶部的是物理学的基本原理，称为 CPT 对称性。

paras.en: CPT stands for charge, parity, and time reversal, three transformations that, when applied together, should leave the fundamental laws of physics unchanged.
paras.zh: CPT 代表电荷、宇称和时间反转，这三种变换一起应用时，应该保持物理基本定律不变。

paras.en: One consequence of this principle is that particles and their antimatter counterparts should have some properties that match exactly.
paras.zh: 这一原理的一个结果是粒子和它们的反物质对应物应该具有一些完全匹配的属性。

paras.en: An electron and a positron, for example, each behave a little like a tiny bar magnet, with a property called a magnetic moment. Their magnetic moments should have equal magnitude but opposite sign.
paras.zh: 例如，电子和正电子的行为都有点像一个微小的条形磁铁，具有称为磁矩的属性。它们的磁矩应大小相等但符号相反。

paras.en: Physicists have already measured the electron's magnetic moment with astonishing precision. Now, thanks to their ability to control a single positron, Gabrielse and his colleagues hope to do the same for its antimatter twin.
paras.zh: 物理学家已经以惊人的精度测量了电子的磁矩。现在，由于他们有能力控制单个正电子，加布里埃尔斯和他的同事希望对其反物质双胞胎做同样的事情。

paras.en: "If the magnitudes are the same, it will be the most precise confirmation of the CPT invariance of the Standard Model – the most fundamental mathematical description of physical reality," Gabrielse explained.
paras.zh: 加布里埃尔斯解释说：“如果大小相同，这将是对标准模型 CPT 不变性的最精确确认——这是物理现实最基本的数学描述。”

paras.en: The researchers are still in the process of obtaining this measurement, and hope to report a result early next year – although given that this is the best opportunity yet to understand a particle so evasive, it could take longer.
paras.zh: 研究人员仍在获得这种测量结果，并希望在明年初报告结果——尽管考虑到这是迄今为止了解如此难以捉摸的粒子的最佳机会，所以可能需要更长时间。

paras.en: Whatever the measurements reveal, they could provide one of the most stringent tests yet of one of the fundamental principles underpinning modern physics.
paras.zh: 无论测量结果如何，它们都可以为支撑现代物理学的基本原理之一提供迄今为止最严格的测试之一。

paras.en: And even if the results agree perfectly with theory, that would leave physicists with some very big questions.
paras.zh: 即使结果与理论完全一致，也会给物理学家留下一些非常大的问题。

paras.en: "It would deepen the mystery of how the Standard Model can make such precise predictions of what we measure, while being inconsistent with basic features of the Universe," Gabrielse said.
paras.zh: 加布里埃尔斯说：“这将加深标准模型如何对我们测量的内容做出如此精确的预测，同时与宇宙的基本特征不一致的谜团。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Physical Review Letters.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《物理评论快报》上。

articles.title: Scientists Transplanted 306 Square Meters of Wild Salt Marsh Into The World's Largest Wave Machine And Let a Simulated Extreme Storm Rip
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: If we really want to know how our coastlines are going to fare under extreme conditions, we're going to need some extreme scientific experiments.
paras.zh: 如果我们真的想知道我们的海岸线在极端条件下会如何，我们将需要一些极端的科学实验。

paras.en: Scientists from the Netherlands have raised the bar, going to great lengths to demonstrate the physical power of salt marshes in the face of massive storm surges.
paras.zh: 来自荷兰的科学家提高了标准，不遗余力地展示盐沼在面对大规模风暴潮时的物理力量。

paras.en: Water engineer Pim Willemsen and his colleagues dug up 306 square meters of a real salt marsh from the coast of the Wadden Sea, and transplanted it into the world's largest wave generator, the Delta Flume.
paras.zh: 水利工程师 Pim Willemsen 和他的同事从瓦登海沿岸挖出了 306 平方米的真正盐沼，并将其移植到世界上最大的波浪发生器 Delta Flume 中。

paras.en: Then, they blasted the 'marsh' with a relentless series of storm waves for 21 hours.
paras.zh: 然后，他们用一系列无情的风暴波袭击了这片“沼泽”，持续了 21 个小时。

paras.en: "We [chose] this quite extraordinary method, because the conditions we wanted to test, and which the dikes in the Netherlands are designed for, do simply not happen in the field [often]," Willemsen told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: “我们选择了这种非常特别的方法，因为我们想要测试的条件以及荷兰堤坝设计的条件，在现场根本不会发生，”威廉森告诉 ScienceAlert。

paras.en: "The dikes are designed to withstand a storm statistically occurring once every thousands of years. We cannot wait for that to happen in the field, so we had to bring the salt marsh to the storm."
paras.zh: “这些堤坝的设计目的是抵御据统计每数千年发生一次的风暴。我们迫不及待地希望这种情况在野外发生，所以我们必须将盐沼带入风暴中。”

paras.en: The results are published today in Nature.
paras.zh: 研究结果今天发表在《自然》杂志上。

paras.en: Setting up this grand experiment was no easy feat.
paras.zh: 开展这项伟大的实验绝非易事。

paras.en: The researchers took great care to ensure the marsh blocks were in more or less the same condition by the time they reached the wave machine.
paras.zh: 研究人员非常小心地确保沼泽块在到达波浪机时处于大致相同的状态。

paras.en: The blocks were dug up from Peazemerlannen nature reserve in September and October 2023. Each block weighed 3,000-6,000 kilograms, including 0.4 to 0.7 meters-deep chunk of soil, as well as the vegetation growing in it (mostly Elymus athericus, some Atriplex species, and Aster tripolium).
paras.zh: 这些石块于2023年9月和10月从Peazemerlannen自然保护区挖出。每个石块重3,000-6,000公斤，包括0.4至0.7米深的土块，以及其中生长的植被（主要是披碱草、一些滨藜属物种和紫菀）。

paras.en: The team transported these blocks in a closed truck to prevent the wind from breaking them apart on the ~250-kilometer journey to the Delta Flume in Delft. They kept a close eye on their weight to ensure they didn't dry out in the process.
paras.zh: 该团队用封闭式卡车运输这些石块，以防止在前往代尔夫特 Delta Flume 的约 250 公里的旅程中风将它们吹散。他们密切关注自己的体重，以确保自己不会在此过程中变干。

paras.en: All of this highlights just how seriously the Netherlands takes its flood control.
paras.zh: 所有这些都凸显了荷兰对防洪工作的重视程度。

paras.en: With a quarter of the country below sea level, the Netherlands has always been at risk of flooding, especially during storm surges. Much of that risk is mitigated by a system of dikes, sea walls, and dams known as the Delta Works.
paras.zh: 荷兰四分之一的国土低于海平面，因此一直面临洪水的风险，尤其是在风暴潮期间。被称为三角洲工程的堤坝、海堤和水坝系统缓解了大部分风险。

paras.en: These 'grey' flood protection measures have worked relatively well through history, but the tides they are a-changin'.
paras.zh: 这些“灰色”防洪措施在历史上相对有效，但潮汐正在发生变化。

paras.en: We humans keep burning fossil fuels, releasing greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. These gases trap enormous amounts of heat, which is fundamentally changing Earth's climate systems.
paras.zh: 我们人类不断燃烧化石燃料，向大气中释放温室气体。这些气体吸收了大量的热量，从根本上改变了地球的气候系统。

paras.en: It's getting hotter, windier, and stormier. Storm surges are driving water levels up much higher than most infrastructure is built for, and it's expected to get worse in the coming decades.
paras.zh: 天气越来越热，风越来越大，暴风雨也越来越大。风暴潮导致水位远远高于大多数基础设施的建设水平，预计未来几十年情况会变得更糟。

paras.en: "Hard engineering structures are static and do not adapt to a changing environment," writes Willemsen and team.
paras.zh: “硬工程结构是静态的，无法适应不断变化的环境，”威廉森和团队写道。

paras.en: Salt marshes, on the other hand, are a little more flexible, as the Delta Flume experiment demonstrates. They have the potential to dissipate wave energy before it reaches the built environment – if we keep them intact.
paras.zh: 另一方面，正如三角洲水槽实验所证明的那样，盐沼更加灵活。如果我们保持它们完好无损，它们有可能在波浪能到达建筑环境之前将其消散。

paras.en: "The salt marsh in the flume was exposed to increasing wave heights from 0.75 meters up to 2 meters," Willemsen told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: “水槽中的盐沼暴露在从 0.75 米到 2 米不断增加的波高中，”威廉森告诉 ScienceAlert。

paras.en: "Depending on the location and local setting, these are water levels and potential wave conditions that occur once every hundred to thousands of years."
paras.zh: “根据地点和当地环境，这些水位和潜在的波浪条件每数百年至数千年发生一次。”

paras.en: Willemsen expected the salt marsh would help absorb some of the wave power.
paras.zh: 威廉森预计盐沼将有助于吸收部分波浪能。

paras.en: Still, he was surprised that after 21 hours of constant battering by waves, the marsh only lost 7 millimeters of sediment.
paras.zh: 但令他惊讶的是，经过21个小时的不断海浪冲击，沼泽地的泥沙只流失了7毫米。

paras.en: After the first wave run, 33 percent of above-ground vegetation biomass was lost, and the damage increased as the wave exposure progressed.
paras.zh: 第一波浪潮过后，33% 的地上植被生物量损失，并且随着波浪暴露的进行，损害不断加剧。

paras.en: After 21 hours, about 20-25 percent of the original above-ground biomass remained. Stem lengths were reduced by 47 percent.
paras.zh: 21 小时后，原来地上生物量的大约 20-25% 仍然存在。茎长度减少了 47%。

paras.en: The vegetation takes damage, but unlike a concrete dike, it can grow back after a storm.
paras.zh: 植被受到破坏，但与混凝土堤坝不同，它可以在暴风雨后重新生长。

paras.en: "It shows that vegetation can contribute to wave attenuation under a wide range of conditions," Willemsen said.
paras.zh: “这表明植被可以在多种条件下促进波浪衰减，”威廉森说。

paras.en: "The marsh is even stronger than we anticipated."
paras.zh: “沼泽地比我们想象的还要强大。”

paras.en: But there are limits to what we can expect of them.
paras.zh: 但我们对它们的期望是有限的。

paras.en: The salt marsh was most effective in low-energy systems, with waves up to 1 meter, attenuating wave power by up to 50 percent. In high-energy systems, with wave heights over 1 meter, attenuation was no more than 10 percent.
paras.zh: 盐沼在低能量系统中最为有效，波浪高达 1 米，波浪能衰减高达 50%。在波高超过 1 米的高能系统中，衰减不超过 10%。

paras.en: In the Netherlands, salt marsh restoration and conservation could be used in tandem with dikes, and may even help to save costs by reducing the need to rebuild or add height to built flood infrastructure.
paras.zh: 在荷兰，盐沼恢复和保护可以与堤坝结合使用，甚至可以通过减少重建或增加已建防洪基础设施的需要来帮助节省成本。

paras.en: "Globally, it shows that there is a large potential of including the marsh with its vegetation in coastal protection schemes as a hybrid coastal defense where dikes and seawalls are combined with a coastal ecosystem," Willemsen said.
paras.zh: 威廉森说：“在全球范围内，这表明将沼泽及其植被纳入沿海保护计划作为混合海岸防御，其中堤坝和海堤与沿海生态系统相结合具有巨大的潜力。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然》杂志上。

articles.title: A train was delayed by a solar storm. But something didn't add up.

paras.en: A train was delayed by a solar storm. But something didn't add up.
paras.zh: 一列火车因太阳风暴而延误。但有些事情并没有加起来。

paras.en: - Scientists have cracked a 178-year-old mystery surrounding a train delayed by a solar storm, revealing that the famous incident happened in 1848 rather than 1841. The discovery rewrites the early history of space weather and highlights a threat that still endangers modern power grids, satellites, and communication systems.
paras.zh: - 科学家破解了围绕一列因太阳风暴延误的火车已有 178 年之久的谜团，揭示了这一著名事件发生在 1848 年而不是 1841 年。这一发现改写了太空天气的早期历史，并凸显了仍然威胁着现代电网、卫星和通信系统的威胁。

paras.en: A mysterious train delay nearly 180 years ago has led scientists to uncover a surprising mistake in the history of space weather. An international research team has solved a 178-year-old mystery involving one of the earliest documented cases of solar activity interfering with electrical technology.
paras.zh: 近 180 年前的一次神秘火车晚点让科学家们发现了太空天气史上的一个令人惊讶的错误。一个国际研究小组解开了一个 178 年之谜，涉及最早记录的太阳活动干扰电力技术的案例之一。

paras.en: The incident dates back to the 1840s, when electric telegraph networks were beginning to transform long-distance communication. As these early systems expanded, operators occasionally encountered strange electrical disturbances that could disrupt their equipment. Scientists now understand that some of these problems were caused by changes in Earth's magnetic field triggered by activity on the Sun.
paras.zh: 该事件可以追溯到 1840 年代，当时电报网络开始改变长途通信。随着这些早期系统的扩展，操作员偶尔会遇到奇怪的电气干扰，可能会破坏他们的设备。科学家们现在了解到，其中一些问题是由太阳活动引发的地球磁场变化引起的。

paras.en: Researchers led by Lancaster University have revisited a historical account of a train delayed in Exeter, England, when solar activity interfered with the railway's telegraph system. The investigation involved scientists from RMIT University, the British Geological Survey, Natural Resources Canada, Baylor University, and the UK's national space laboratory, RAL Space.
paras.zh: 由兰卡斯特大学领导的研究人员重新审视了英国埃克塞特一列火车延误的历史记录，当时太阳活动干扰了铁路的电报系统。这项调查涉及来自皇家墨尔本理工大学、英国地质调查局、加拿大自然资源部、贝勒大学和英国国家太空实验室 RAL Space 的科学家。

paras.en: By piecing together historical documents and scientific observations, the team uncovered an error that changes the timeline of the earliest known technological disruptions caused by space weather.
paras.zh: 通过将历史文献和科学观察拼凑在一起，该团队发现了一个错误，该错误改变了由太空天气引起的最早已知技术中断的时间线。

paras.en: How Solar Storms First Disrupted Technology
paras.zh: 太阳风暴如何首先扰乱技术

paras.en: One of history's most dramatic examples of space weather affecting technology occurred in 1859. Known as the Carrington Event, the powerful solar storm involved a massive solar flare and a coronal mass ejection, an enormous eruption of charged particles and magnetic fields from the Sun.
paras.zh: 历史上最引人注目的太空天气影响技术的例子之一发生在 1859 年。这场强大的太阳风暴被称为卡林顿事件，涉及大规模太阳耀斑和日冕物质抛射，即来自太阳的带电粒子和磁场的巨大喷发。

paras.en: The resulting disturbances produced spectacular auroras, commonly known as the northern lights, that appeared as far south as Hawaii and Central America. In some locations, the sky glowed brightly enough for people to read newspapers at night. The unusual illumination even fooled gold miners into thinking morning had arrived, prompting them to prepare breakfast shortly after midnight.
paras.zh: 由此产生的扰动产生了壮观的极光，通常称为北极光，其出现远至夏威夷和中美洲南部。在某些地方，天空发出明亮的光芒，人们可以在夜间阅读报纸。这种不寻常的照明甚至让金矿工人误以为早晨已经到来，促使他们在午夜过后不久准备早餐。

paras.en: The storm also wreaked havoc on telegraph networks around the world. Electrical surges caused equipment failures, sent sparks flying from wires, shocked operators, and even started fires. In some cases, the electrical currents generated by the disturbance were so powerful that telegraph systems continued operating without batteries.
paras.zh: 这场风暴还对世界各地的电报网络造成严重破坏。电涌会导致设备故障、电线中飞出火花、电击操作人员，甚至引发火灾。在某些情况下，干扰产生的电流非常强大，以至于电报系统无需电池即可继续运行。

paras.en: Although the Carrington Event remains the most famous example from this period, evidence of solar activity interfering with electrical systems stretches back even further.
paras.zh: 尽管卡灵顿事件仍然是这一时期最著名的例子，但太阳活动干扰电力系统的证据可以追溯到更早的时候。

paras.en: In 1871, an anonymous author published an account in the scientific journal Nature describing a "very intense magnetic disturbance" that supposedly occurred on October 18, 1841. According to the report, the disturbance interfered with railway signals in Exeter and delayed the scheduled 10:05 p.m. train departure by 16 minutes.
paras.zh: 1871 年，一位匿名作者在科学杂志《自然》上发表了一篇报道，描述了据称发生于 1841 年 10 月 18 日的“非常强烈的磁扰”。报告称，这次扰动干扰了埃克塞特的铁路信号，导致原定晚上 10 点 05 分延误。火车 16 分钟发车。

paras.en: If the date had been correct, the event would have represented the earliest known instance of space weather disrupting human technology.
paras.zh: 如果日期正确，该事件将代表已知最早的太空天气扰乱人类技术的实例。

paras.en: However, a new investigation published in the American Geophysical Union journal Space Weather has revealed that the original account contained a significant historical error.
paras.zh: 然而，美国地球物理联盟杂志《太空天气》上发表的一项新调查显示，原始描述存在重大历史错误。

paras.en: The Railway Mystery That Changed Solar Storm History
paras.zh: 改变太阳风暴历史的铁路之谜

paras.en: Associate Professor Brett Carter, a space weather researcher at RMIT University, helped investigate the historical records. During the investigation, the team noticed a problem that immediately called the original timeline into question.
paras.zh: 皇家墨尔本理工大学空间天气研究员布雷特·卡特副教授帮助调查了历史记录。在调查过程中，团队发现了一个问题，立即使原来的时间表受到质疑。

paras.en: The Exeter-to-Starcross railway line mentioned in the report did not open until 1846, almost five years after the event supposedly occurred.
paras.zh: 报告中提到的埃克塞特至斯塔克罗斯铁路线直到 1846 年才开通，即事件发生近五年后。

paras.en: "In this study, we effectively investigated what had to be a typo in a Nature paper from 1871. We know it was a typo because the Exeter-to-Starcross train line mentioned in that paper didn't exist until 1846, which is 5 years afterwards," he said.
paras.zh: “在这项研究中，我们有效地调查了 1871 年《自然》杂志论文中的拼写错误。我们知道这是一个拼写错误，因为该论文中提到的埃克塞特到斯塔克罗斯的火车线路直到 1846 年才存在，也就是 5 年后，”他说。

paras.en: To establish when the train delay actually happened, the researchers examined a wide range of historical evidence. They compared railway timetables and newspaper reports with observations of solar activity, accounts of auroras, and digitized measurements of Earth's magnetic field.
paras.zh: 为了确定火车晚点实际发生的时间，研究人员检查了广泛的历史证据。他们将铁路时刻表和报纸报道与太阳活动的观测、极光的描述以及地球磁场的数字化测量进行了比较。

paras.en: Together, these records pointed to a different date: October 18, 1848, exactly seven years later than originally reported.
paras.zh: 这些记录加在一起指向了一个不同的日期：1848 年 10 月 18 日，比最初报道的晚了整整七年。

paras.en: The revised timeline resolves the apparent contradiction and places the incident during an important period in technological history, when electrical communication systems were becoming increasingly widespread.
paras.zh: 修订后的时间表解决了明显的矛盾，并将该事件置于技术史上的一个重要时期，当时电气通信系统变得越来越普遍。

paras.en: Carter explained that the 1840s marked a turning point in humanity's relationship with space weather. Solar disturbances had always occurred, but the emergence of electrical technology meant that their effects could now interfere directly with everyday human activities.
paras.zh: 卡特解释说，1840 年代标志着人类与太空天气关系的转折点。太阳干扰一直存在，但电力技术的出现意味着它们的影响现在可以直接干扰人类的日常活动。

paras.en: "Understanding this historical event is important because the 1840s mark the intersection between the rise of our technological age and space weather, which has always been around," Carter says.
paras.zh: “了解这一历史事件非常重要，因为 1840 年代标志着我们的技术时代的兴起与太空天气之间的交集，而太空天气一直存在，”卡特说。

paras.en: "Since this line was crossed, humans have not looked back."
paras.zh: “自从越过这条线以来，人类就没有回头。”

paras.en: The findings also change the incident's place in the historical record. Although the Exeter disruption remains one of the earliest credible examples of space weather affecting technology, it can no longer be considered the first.
paras.zh: 研究结果还改变了该事件在历史记录中的地位。尽管埃克塞特的破坏仍然是太空天气影响技术最早的可靠例子之一，但它不再被认为是第一个。

paras.en: That distinction now belongs to an earlier documented incident involving telegraph interference on Britain's Midland Railway in March 1847.
paras.zh: 这一区别现在属于较早记录的事件，涉及 1847 年 3 月对英国米德兰铁路的电报干扰。

paras.en: Professor Jim Wild of Lancaster University, who led the study, said the findings demonstrate that the dangers associated with space weather began affecting society long before the development of modern power grids, satellites, and electronic communication networks.
paras.zh: 领导这项研究的兰卡斯特大学教授吉姆·怀尔德表示，研究结果表明，与太空天气相关的危险早在现代电网、卫星和电子通信网络发展之前就开始影响社会。

paras.en: "What this research highlights is that space weather is not a new threat but a long-standing natural hazard. Society has been experiencing the effects of space weather on technology for almost as long as electrical technologies have existed," Wild said.
paras.zh: “这项研究强调的是，太空天气不是一种新的威胁，而是一种长期存在的自然灾害。几乎自从电气技术存在以来，社会就一直在经历太空天气对技术的影响，”怀尔德说。

paras.en: The Exeter incident is especially significant because it occurred when electrical technology was still in its infancy. Early railway operators were beginning to rely on telegraph systems, creating new opportunities for solar disturbances to interfere with essential infrastructure.
paras.zh: 埃克塞特事件尤为重要，因为它发生时电气技术仍处于起步阶段。早期的铁路运营商开始依赖电报系统，这为太阳扰动干扰重要基础设施创造了新的机会。

paras.en: "The Exeter train delay is a fascinating story because it sits right at the point where emerging technologies first began to encounter the realities of the space environment. By combining historical archives with scientific observations, we've been able to show that the event almost certainly happened in 1848 rather than 1841.
paras.zh: “埃克塞特火车延误是一个引人入胜的故事，因为它正好处于新兴技术首次开始遭遇太空环境现实的时刻。通过将历史档案与科学观察相结合，我们已经能够证明该事件几乎肯定发生在 1848 年，而不是 1841 年。

paras.en: "Although this means it is not the earliest recorded space weather impact, it remains one of the first clear examples of solar activity disrupting critical infrastructure," he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“尽管这意味着这不是最早有记录的太空天气影响，但它仍然是太阳活动破坏关键基础设施的第一个明显例子之一。”

paras.en: The investigation also shows how historical scientific records can be used alongside newspapers and other archival materials to reconstruct events that occurred long before modern monitoring instruments became available.
paras.zh: 这项调查还展示了如何将历史科学记录与报纸和其他档案材料一起使用，以重建远在现代监测仪器出现之前发生的事件。

paras.en: "It also demonstrates the value of combining scientific records with contemporary newspaper reports and archival documents when reconstructing historic space weather events."
paras.zh: “它还展示了在重建历史性太空天气事件时将科学记录与当代报纸报道和档案文件相结合的价值。”

paras.en: Dr. Mike Hapgood, a Visiting Scientist and space weather expert at the UK's national space laboratory, RAL Space, described the research process as something resembling a detective investigation.
paras.zh: 英国国家太空实验室 RAL Space 的访问科学家兼太空气象专家迈克·哈普古德 (Mike Hapgood) 博士将研究过程描述为类似于侦探调查。

paras.en: "It highlights the importance of preserving these older records, which give us the evidence base we need to interpret past events and strengthen future predictions," he said.
paras.zh: “它强调了保存这些较旧记录的重要性，这些记录为我们提供了解释过去事件和加强未来预测所需的证据基础，”他说。

paras.en: Modern Technology Still Faces the Threat of Solar Storms
paras.zh: 现代技术仍然面临太阳风暴的威胁

paras.en: Almost two centuries after the Exeter train delay, solar storms continue to pose risks to railways and other essential infrastructure. The technologies involved have changed dramatically, but they remain susceptible to disturbances originating from the Sun.
paras.zh: 埃克塞特火车延误近两个世纪后，太阳风暴继续对铁路和其他重要基础设施构成风险。所涉及的技术已经发生了巨大的变化，但它们仍然容易受到来自太阳的干扰。

paras.en: Today, space weather can interfere with electrical power systems, railway signaling equipment, satellite navigation, and communication networks. Powerful solar events can disturb Earth's magnetic field, potentially generating unwanted electrical currents in infrastructure and affecting systems that depend on reliable satellite signals.
paras.zh: 如今，太空天气会干扰电力系统、铁路信号设备、卫星导航和通信网络。强大的太阳活动可能会扰乱地球磁场，可能会在基础设施中产生不需要的电流，并影响依赖可靠卫星信号的系统。

paras.en: Scientists now have far more sophisticated instruments and forecasting methods than were available in the 19th century. However, Hapgood emphasized that modern society's growing dependence on interconnected electrical and space technologies also creates new vulnerabilities.
paras.zh: 现在，科学家们拥有比 19 世纪更加先进的仪器和预测方法。然而，哈普古德强调，现代社会对互联电力和空间技术的日益依赖也造成了新的脆弱性。

paras.en: Understanding how past solar storms affected infrastructure can help researchers assess the dangers posed by future events and develop better ways to reduce potential disruptions.
paras.zh: 了解过去的太阳风暴如何影响基础设施可以帮助研究人员评估未来事件带来的危险，并开发更好的方法来减少潜在的破坏。

paras.en: "Deepening our understanding of these events is essential for preparing for, and mitigating, the impacts of space weather - especially as we look forward to a decade of exciting space developments that will face the challenge of a new solar cycle in the 2030s," he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“加深我们对这些事件的理解对于准备和减轻太空天气的影响至关重要，特别是当我们期待着十年令人兴奋的太空发展，并将面临 2030 年代新太阳周期的挑战时。”

paras.en: Materials provided by RMIT University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由皇家墨尔本理工大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - James A. Wild, Ciaran D. Beggan, David H. Boteler, William B. Cade, Brett A. Carter, Michael Hapgood. Did Space Weather Delay the 10:05 p.m. Train Departure From Exeter on 18 October 1841? Space Weather, 2026; 24 (9) DOI: 10.1029/2026SW005239
paras.zh: - 詹姆斯·A·怀尔德、塞兰·D·贝根、大卫·H·波特勒、威廉·B·凯德、布雷特·A·卡特、迈克尔·哈普古德。太空天气是否推迟了晚上 10 点 05 分的时间？ 1841 年 10 月 18 日火车从埃克塞特出发？太空天气，2026； 24 (9) DOI: 10.1029/2026SW005239

articles.title: Too much RNA can starve cells of energy, scientists discover

paras.en: Too much RNA can starve cells of energy, scientists discover
paras.zh: 科学家发现过多的RNA会使细胞缺乏能量

paras.en: - Scientists have uncovered an unexpected danger lurking inside cells: too much RNA can damage the structures responsible for producing energy. A new study found that excess RNA, including the normally essential messenger RNA (mRNA), can directly disrupt mitochondria without relying on the immune system. The discovery could help explain how viral infections and certain aging-related diseases damage cells.
paras.zh: - 科学家们发现细胞内潜伏着一个意想不到的危险：过多的RNA会损害负责产生能量的结构。一项新研究发现，过量的 RNA，包括通常必需的信使 RNA (mRNA)，可以直接破坏线粒体，而不依赖于免疫系统。这一发现可能有助于解释病毒感染和某些与衰老相关的疾病如何损害细胞。

paras.en: Scientists have uncovered a surprising way that viruses can interfere with the body's cells. When too much RNA accumulates inside a cell, it can damage the structures that produce energy, potentially leaving the cell struggling to function normally.
paras.zh: 科学家发现了病毒干扰人体细胞的一种令人惊讶的方式。当细胞内积累过多的 RNA 时，它会损害产生能量的结构，可能导致细胞难以正常运作。

paras.en: A new study led by researchers at the Texas A&M College of Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences (VMBS) found that excess RNA produced during poxvirus infections can impair mitochondria, the tiny structures responsible for generating most of the energy cells need to survive.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯农工大学兽医与生物医学科学学院 (VMBS) 的研究人员领导的一项新研究发现，痘病毒感染期间产生的过量 RNA 会损害线粒体，而线粒体是负责产生细胞生存所需的大部分能量的微小结构。

paras.en: Published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the research reveals an unexpected connection between RNA buildup and cellular energy production. The findings could have implications far beyond viral infections, potentially helping scientists better understand aging-related diseases and improve RNA-based medical treatments, including mRNA vaccines.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上，揭示了 RNA 积累和细胞能量产生之间的意外联系。这些发现的影响可能远远超出病毒感染范围，可能有助于科学家更好地了解与衰老相关的疾病，并改进基于 RNA 的医疗方法，包括 mRNA 疫苗。

paras.en: "Scientists have long known that RNA degradation helps control protein production and remove defective RNA," said Dr. Zhilong Yang, a professor in VMBS' Department of Veterinary Pathobiology. "Our study reveals another important role: it helps cells maintain the energy they need to function properly."
paras.zh: VMBS 兽医病理学系教授杨志龙博士说：“科学家们早就知道 RNA 降解有助于控制蛋白质的产生并去除有缺陷的 RNA。” “我们的研究揭示了另一个重要作用：它帮助细胞维持正常运作所需的能量。”

paras.en: Cells constantly produce and break down RNA as part of their normal activities. This cleanup process, known as RNA degradation, helps regulate protein production, eliminate faulty RNA, and control immune responses. The new findings suggest it also performs another essential function by protecting the cell's energy supply.
paras.zh: 作为其正常活动的一部分，细胞不断产生和分解 RNA。这种清理过程称为 RNA 降解，有助于调节蛋白质的产生、消除有缺陷的 RNA 并控制免疫反应。新发现表明它还通过保护细胞的能量供应来发挥另一项重要功能。

paras.en: RNA plays several important roles in keeping cells functioning. Messenger RNA (mRNA), for example, carries genetic instructions that tell cells which proteins to produce. These proteins are needed for nearly everything cells do, from maintaining their structure to carrying out essential chemical reactions.
paras.zh: RNA 在维持细胞功能方面发挥着多种重要作用。例如，信使 RNA (mRNA) 携带遗传指令，告诉细胞要产生哪些蛋白质。细胞几乎所有的活动都需要这些蛋白质，从维持结构到进行必要的化学反应。

paras.en: Another type, double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), frequently appears during viral infections. Its presence can serve as a warning signal, alerting the immune system that a virus may have entered the cell.
paras.zh: 另一种类型是双链RNA (dsRNA)，经常出现在病毒感染期间。它的存在可以作为警告信号，提醒免疫系统病毒可能已进入细胞。

paras.en: Viruses often generate large quantities of RNA as they reproduce inside infected cells. Ordinarily, cellular cleanup systems help prevent RNA from accumulating to harmful levels. However, when RNA production exceeds the cell's ability to break it down, the excess material can interfere with mitochondria and reduce energy production.
paras.zh: 病毒在受感染的细胞内繁殖时通常会产生大量 RNA。通常，细胞清理系统有助于防止 RNA 积累到有害水平。然而，当 RNA 的产生超过细胞分解它的能力时，多余的物质会干扰线粒体并减少能量产生。

paras.en: Scientists already understood that excessive double-stranded RNA could provoke potentially harmful immune responses. What surprised the researchers was discovering that too much ordinary messenger RNA could also damage mitochondria.
paras.zh: 科学家们已经了解到，过量的双链 RNA 可能会引发潜在有害的免疫反应。令研究人员惊讶的是，过多的普通信使 RNA 也会损伤线粒体。

paras.en: "MRNA is a normal component of our cells, but it seems like with many good things, if we get too much, that can become a problem for the cell," Yang said. "When too much RNA builds up, including mRNA, it can damage the mitochondria and interfere with the cell's ability to produce energy."
paras.zh: “mRNA 是我们细胞的正常成分，但似乎很多好东西，如果我们摄入太多，就会给细胞带来问题，”Yang 说。 “当过多的 RNA（包括 mRNA）积累时，它会损害线粒体并干扰细胞产生能量的能力。”

paras.en: This creates an unusual challenge for viruses. Although viruses depend entirely on the cells they infect to supply energy and manufacture proteins, producing excessive amounts of viral RNA can damage the very machinery they need to reproduce.
paras.zh: 这给病毒带来了不寻常的挑战。尽管病毒完全依赖它们感染的细胞来提供能量和制造蛋白质，但产生过量的病毒 RNA 会损害它们繁殖所需的机器。

paras.en: According to Yang, poxviruses, a group that includes the viruses responsible for smallpox and mpox, appear to have ways of managing this problem. They use RNA cleanup mechanisms to remove excess RNA, helping infected cells remain functional long enough for viral replication to continue.
paras.zh: 据杨介绍，痘病毒（包括引起天花和 MPOX 的病毒）似乎有办法解决这个问题。他们使用 RNA 清理机制来去除多余的 RNA，帮助受感染的细胞保持功能足够长的时间，以便病毒继续复制。

paras.en: "If the cell is not healthy, the virus would not replicate well," Yang said. "The virus needs to keep RNA levels balanced inside the cell."
paras.zh: “如果细胞不健康，病毒就无法很好地复制，”杨说。 “病毒需要保持细胞内 RNA 水平的平衡。”

paras.en: Scientists Discover RNA Can Directly Damage Mitochondria
paras.zh: 科学家发现RNA可以直接损伤线粒体

paras.en: One of the study's most unexpected findings emerged when researchers investigated exactly how excess RNA affects mitochondria.
paras.zh: 当研究人员准确调查过量的 RNA 如何影响线粒体时，该研究最意想不到的发现之一出现了。

paras.en: Initially, the team suspected that RNA buildup was damaging these cellular powerhouses indirectly by activating the immune system. Certain types of RNA are known to trigger defensive responses, which can place additional stress on infected cells.
paras.zh: 最初，研究小组怀疑 RNA 的积累通过激活免疫系统间接损害这些细胞动力源。已知某些类型的 RNA 会引发防御反应，这会给受感染的细胞带来额外的压力。

paras.en: However, experiments revealed that the damage did not require an immune response.
paras.zh: 然而，实验表明这种损伤并不需要免疫反应。

paras.en: "When we isolated only the mitochondria and added RNA, we still saw mitochondrial damage," said Dr. Djamal Brahim Belhaouari, the study's first author. "That was the moment we realized this could be a previously unknown cellular response to RNA."
paras.zh: “当我们只分离线粒体并添加 RNA 时，我们仍然看到线粒体损伤，”该研究的第一作者 Djamal Brahim Belhaouari 博士说。 “就在那时我们意识到这可能是一种以前未知的细胞对 RNA 的反应。”

paras.en: The researchers also observed that mitochondrial problems developed before substantial immune activation occurred. Furthermore, the damage did not depend on the immune pathways normally activated during infection.
paras.zh: 研究人员还观察到，线粒体问题在大量免疫激活发生之前就已经出现。此外，损害并不取决于感染期间通常激活的免疫途径。
