Details of help available in many countries can be found at Befrienders Worldwide, external, external.

articles.title: US envoy to meet Putin in Russia as Zelensky says intelligence sharing 'works now'

paras.en: US special envoy Steve Witkoff is set to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss proposals on ending Russia's years-long conflict with Ukraine.
paras.zh: 美国特使史蒂夫·维特科夫（ Steve Witkoff ）将于周三在圣彼得堡会见俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京（ Vladimir Putin ） ，讨论结束俄罗斯与乌克兰长达数年的冲突的建议。

paras.en: The talks come one day after Witkoff's meeting with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo, which a US official described as "constructive".
paras.zh: 会谈是在维特科夫与乌克兰总统沃洛季米尔·泽伦斯基（ Volodymyr Zelensky ）在奥斯陆会晤后的一天举行的，一位美国官员称之为“建设性的”。

paras.en: Kyiv previously accused the US of withholding key intelligence - a claim rejected as "scandalous" by Washington - but on Tuesday, Zelensky said that intelligence sharing with the US on Russian missile attacks "works now".
paras.zh: 基辅此前曾指责美国隐瞒关键情报-华盛顿以“丑闻”为由拒绝了这一说法-但泽伦斯基周二表示，与美国就俄罗斯导弹袭击进行情报共享“现在起作用了”。

paras.en: Zelensky and his European allies said it was now up to Russia to respond to the proposals agreed in Oslo when Witkoff meets Putin on Wednesday.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基和他的欧洲盟友表示，现在应该由俄罗斯来回应维特科夫周三与普京会晤时在奥斯陆商定的提案。

paras.en: Finnish President Alexander Stubb, who also took part in the talks, said "genuine progress" was made on proposals to achieve peace but gave no details and warned that patience would be needed.
paras.zh: 芬兰总统亚历山大·斯图布（ Alexander Stubb ）也参加了会谈，他说，在实现和平的建议上取得了“真正的进展” ，但没有提供任何细节，并警告说需要耐心。

paras.en: Witkoff was not present at the joint press conference after Tuesday's talks in the Norwegian capital. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, another key envoy, took part in the meeting via video link.
paras.zh: 周二在挪威首都举行会谈后， Witkoff没有出席联合新闻发布会。特朗普的女婿贾里德·库什纳（ Jared Kushner ）是另一位重要的特使，他通过视频链接参加了会议。

paras.en: A US official later described the talks as "very productive and constructive", saying there was a "strong alignment at the working level" among the US, Ukraine and Europe on "the next steps".
paras.zh: 一位美国官员后来形容会谈“非常富有成效和建设性” ，称美国、乌克兰和欧洲在“下一步措施”上“在工作层面上有很强的一致性”。

paras.en: The official confirmed that Witkoff is due to meet President Vladimir Putin in Russia tomorrow to discuss the proposals and that Kushner will again participate virtually.
paras.zh: 这位官员证实，维特科夫将于明天在俄罗斯会见弗拉基米尔·普京总统，讨论这些提议，库什纳将再次以虚拟方式参与。

paras.en: Putin is yet to publicly comment on the latest developments, but Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov earlier said the Kremlin would listen to what Wiktoff would offer, while ruling out "any political concessions".
paras.zh: 普京尚未公开评论最新事态发展，但外交部长谢尔盖·拉夫罗夫早些时候表示，克里姆林宫将听取维克托夫的意见，同时排除“任何政治让步”。

paras.en: Relations between Ukraine and the US have soured in recent weeks to the extent that Trump has said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president, and most recently "for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine".
paras.zh: 最近几周，乌克兰和美国之间的关系恶化，以至于特朗普表示，现在是乌克兰选出新总统的时候了，最近一次是“让其他人代表乌克兰进行谈判”。

paras.en: Ahead of next month's US midterm elections, Trump has also sought to blame Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries for fuel prices which have been rising since the start of the US-led war on Iran.
paras.zh: 在下个月的美国中期选举之前，特朗普还试图将乌克兰对俄罗斯炼油厂的袭击归咎于自美国领导的伊朗战争开始以来一直在上涨的燃料价格。

paras.en: Speaking after Zelensky's news conference in Oslo, Trump again told reporters at the White House he wanted Kyiv to "make a deal". He said Russia would like to "get it done" and it was "time for Ukraine to end this war".
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基在奥斯陆举行新闻发布会后，特朗普再次在白宫对记者说，他希望基辅“达成协议”。他说，俄罗斯希望“完成这项工作” ，现在是“乌克兰结束这场战争的时候了”。

paras.en: Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.
paras.zh: 普京于2022年发动了对乌克兰的全面入侵，莫斯科目前控制着乌克兰约20 ％的领土。

paras.en: Russian drone attacks have continued this week. Ukrainian officials said at least 10 people were killed on Tuesday - four in Kyiv and the capital region, another four in the eastern Donetsk region, and two in the central city of Dnipro. Another attack overnight on Wednesday killed two more people near Kharkiv, the country's second-largest city.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯无人机袭击本周仍在继续。乌克兰官员表示，周二至少有10人遇难，其中4人在基辅和首都地区， 4人在顿涅茨克东部地区， 2人在第聂伯罗市中心。周三晚上发生的另一起袭击事件在该国第二大城市哈尔科夫附近又造成两人死亡。

paras.en: Addressing the issue of US intelligence sharing after Tuesday's talks, Zelensky said he was "thankful that intelligence works now".
paras.zh: 在周二会谈后，泽伦斯基在谈到美国情报共享问题时表示，他“感谢情报现在发挥作用”。

paras.en: "Speaking about early warning, which is very important for our people, our children, adults, civilians because we can hear when ballistic[s] is coming - so we are thankful to American side, now it works, it's great," the Ukrainian president said.
paras.zh: “谈到早期预警，这对我们的人民，我们的孩子，成年人，平民非常重要，因为我们可以听到弹道导弹何时到来-所以我们感谢美国方面，现在它起作用了，这很棒，”乌克兰总统说。

paras.en: He said he also hoped for a good result on SpaceX's Starlink satellite access as well, after Ukraine's military had reported in recent days speed restrictions on the US platform used by Kyiv to carry out drone strikes against Russia.
paras.zh: 他说，他还希望SpaceX的Starlink卫星接入也能取得好结果，因为乌克兰军方最近几天报告了基辅使用的美国平台对俄罗斯进行无人机袭击的速度限制。

paras.en: Before the Oslo talks, Zelensky said he had had a "constructive discussion" with Rubio about the need for US early warnings, missile interceptors and Starlink.
paras.zh: 在奥斯陆会谈之前，泽伦斯基表示，他与卢比奥就美国早期预警、导弹拦截器和Starlink的必要性进行了“建设性讨论”。

paras.en: Last week, a bipartisan group of US senators called for an urgent investigation into speed restrictions to the Starlink network in Ukraine.
paras.zh: 上周，一个由美国两党参议员组成的小组呼吁对乌克兰Starlink网络的速度限制进行紧急调查。

paras.en: And Zelensky also restated that Ukraine was "ready for negotiations" to end the war.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基还重申，乌克兰“已准备好进行谈判”以结束战争。

paras.en: "Of course, we are not losing this war, but we are losing people because Russia attacks," he said.
paras.zh: “当然，我们不会输掉这场战争，但我们正在失去人民，因为俄罗斯的袭击，”他说。

paras.en: The Ukrainian leader added that "strong" security guarantees for Ukraine were also discussed in Oslo, as well as energy ceasefire proposals.
paras.zh: 这位乌克兰领导人补充说，在奥斯陆也讨论了对乌克兰的“强有力”安全保障，以及能源停火提案。

paras.en: Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re, who also took part in the talks, stressed that Europe "needs to be at the table" during any discussions about how to end the Russia-Ukraine war.
paras.zh: 挪威首相若纳斯·加尔·斯泰雷（ Jonas Gahr Stére ）也参加了会谈，他强调，在关于如何结束俄乌战争的任何讨论中，欧洲“需要站在谈判桌上”。

paras.en: Unconfirmed reports earlier on Tuesday said the transfer of more US-made Patriot interceptor missiles - the only effective weapon in shooting down Russian ballistic missiles - had not yet been approved.
paras.zh: 周二早些时候未经证实的报道称，更多美国制造的爱国者拦截导弹（击落俄罗斯弹道导弹的唯一有效武器）的转让尚未获得批准。

paras.en: Rubio, who is currently on a visit to India, admitted to reporters that it may be true that Patriot interceptors had not yet arrived in Ukraine - but he stressed that nothing had been denied to Kyiv intentionally.
paras.zh: 卢比奥目前正在访问印度，他向记者承认，爱国者拦截机可能还没有抵达乌克兰，但他强调说，基辅没有故意否认任何事情。

paras.en: European leaders meanwhile have expressed concern about recent US statements from the US towards Russia.
paras.zh: 与此同时，欧洲领导人对美国最近对俄罗斯的言论表示担忧。

paras.en: On Monday, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz spoke of "mixed pictures and messages" on the war, adding that he was trying to convince the American government "in total that this is something we have to resolve jointly".
paras.zh: 周一，德国总理弗里德里希·默茨（ Friedrich Merz ）谈到了有关战争的“混合图片和信息” ，并补充说，他试图说服美国政府“总的来说，这是我们必须共同解决的问题”。

paras.en: "It's really a big effort for our budgets, it's really a big thing for the European Union, but we are doing that and we are trying to keep on doing that until this terrible war ends," the German leader told Bloomberg TV.
paras.zh: 这位德国领导人告诉彭博电视台： “这对我们的预算来说确实是一项巨大的努力，对欧盟来说确实是一件大事，但我们正在这样做，我们正在努力继续这样做，直到这场可怕的战争结束。”

paras.en: Asked during an interview on Monday whether or not he saw Ukraine as a US ally, US Vice-President JD Vance said Kyiv was "certainly a partner in some ways, but we have some divergent interests from time to time, like for example... I think they should stop bombing Russian energy".
paras.zh: 在周一的一次采访中，当被问及他是否认为乌克兰是美国的盟友时，美国副总统万斯表示，基辅“在某些方面肯定是一个伙伴，但我们不时有一些不同的利益，比如……我认为他们应该停止轰炸俄罗斯的能源”。

paras.en: "We don't have a formal alliance as far as I know with Ukraine. They're not in Nato, I don't think they should be in Nato... we're gonna work together on some things, but also we're going to be opposite on some things too," he said.
paras.zh: “据我所知，我们与乌克兰没有正式的联盟。他们不在北约，我认为他们不应该在北约......我们将在一些事情上共同努力，但我们在一些事情上也会相反，“他说。

articles.title: CELEBRATING 100 YEARS

paras.en: MEDINA, OH (January 6, 2025) – Carlisle Brake & Friction (CarlisleCBF), a global leader in brake and friction technology and part of the CentroMotion family of brands, has reached a momentous milestone – its 100th anniversary.
Since its founding in 1925, the company has lived up to its tagline, "Braking New Ground," by consistently pioneering innovative solutions that have propelled industries forward.

"For 100 years, Carlisle has been synonymous with groundbreaking innovation and unwavering reliability in the braking industry," says Tom Vanderlaan, Chief Commercial Officer (CCO) of CentroMotion. "This milestone is a testament to the dedication of our employees, the trust of our customers, and the enduring strength of our products. As we celebrate our centennial, we reaffirm our commitment to continuous innovation, strong partnerships, and giving back to the communities we serve."
A Century of Innovation in Motion Control

For a century, CarlisleCBF has been at the forefront of motion control, pushing the boundaries of performance with its industry-leading brakes and friction materials. Through unwavering commitment to R&D, the company has earned the trust of customers worldwide, establishing itself as a cornerstone of reliability.
Celebrating 100 Years of Braking New Ground: A Digital Celebration

To commemorate this historic milestone, CarlisleCBF is launching a comprehensive digital celebration. This virtual experience will allow customers, employees and industry partners to delve into the company’s rich history, groundbreaking innovations and commitment to excellence through historical photographs and stories.

A core aspect of the celebration is fostering a sense of community. CarlisleCBF invites customers, employees and industry partners to join the journey by visiting their dedicated anniversary webpage, www.CarlisleCBF.com, and following their story on social media.
The webpage and social media channels will serve as a virtual time capsule, showcasing CarlisleCBF's rich history, ground-breaking milestones and product innovations.

To encourage participation and celebrate the impact CarlisleCBF has had, a social media campaign is launching with the hashtag #CarlisleCBF100. Participants are encouraged to share stories, photos and memories that illustrate how CarlisleCBF products have impacted their lives or businesses. The most engaging submissions will be featured on the company's social media channels and website.
By combining digital storytelling with interactive social media, CarlisleCBF aims to create a lasting legacy for its first century of service, while fostering a spirit of community and appreciation.

Carlisle Brake & Friction, a CentroMotion brand, is a globally recognized leader in the development and manufacture of highly innovative brake and friction system solutions to service a diverse range of motion control applications. The comprehensive nature of CarlisleCBF's brake system expertise includes hydraulic control products, industrial brake assemblies, and wet and dry friction material for brake, clutch, and transmission applications, as well as aftermarket replacement products. Our full-system product offering, supported by our industry-experience staff of experts, provides our customers with brake system solutions that set them apart from their competition. www.carlislecbf.com

paras.en: CentroMotion designs and delivers highly engineered products that enhance the safety, reliability and productivity of equipment used in transportation, agriculture, construction, mining and demanding industrial environments. Our innovative team works collaboratively with customers through our family of trusted, established brands, bringing deep subject-matter expertise in complementary technologies.

This expertise, combined with our exceptional scale and geographic reach, makes us a reliable partner to help our customers achieve their goals, and provide end users with the best equipment possible. Our well-known brands include Power-Packer for hydraulic motion control and stabilization systems; CrossControl and maximatecc for operator information and human-machine interface systems; Elliott Manufacturing and Weasler Engineering for power and force transmission through flexible and rigid driveline systems; Gits Manufacturing for high-performance engine thermal and emission control solutions; and Carlisle Brake & Friction for materials and mechatronic solutions for off-highway brake and transmission products. paras.en: Carlisle Brake & Friction is one of five CentroMotion brands exhibiting at bauma, April 7–13 in Munich, booth A2, 402.
CentroMotion is a global manufacturing company specializing in friction, information and controls, mechanical power transmission, and thermal and motion control products.

Sharing product highlights from their industry-leading brake, transmissions/clutch and motion control systems.
Showcasing display and on-board computing platforms.

Demonstrating micro-controller-based platforms for instrumentation and HMI.

articles.title: Visit Us @Agritechnica 2025

paras.en: CarlisleCBF is one of seven CentroMotion brands exhibiting at Agritechnica, November 9 - 15, 2025, in Hanover, Germany, stand No. B35, hall 17.
CentroMotion is a global manufacturing company specializing in friction, information, and controls, mechanical power transmission, and thermal and motion control products.
Our teams will showcase various products that serve the agriculture market:

Sharing a powerful lineup of brake system solutions engineered for the demands of modern agriculture equipment. Attendees can explore highlights from industry-leading brake assemblies, designed to deliver unmatched stopping power and durability in off-highway environments. The display will also feature both the EPD and N680 advanced friction technologies, built to optimize performance and reliability in high-torque applications. Together, these products represent a century of engineering excellence and a future-focused commitment to solving the toughest challenges in agricultural mobility.

paras.en: Showcasing the leading on-board computing platform for machine intelligence and HMI solutions. New products, designed specifically to meet the needs of agricultural machinery, include 10- and 12-inch smart terminals, central vehicle computing with monitors, and 5- and 7-inch displays featuring programmable soft keys for tactile control. The CCpilot V1090 and V1290 are the first displays with an integrated network switch that makes it easier to incorporate elements like camera systems, sensors and precision systems, into one display computer. Presenting the latest solutions to help operators sense, see and know more. Show attendees will find a broad portfolio of products, including displays, clusters and sensors for vehicle and equipment monitoring in demanding applications. articles.title: CCC Advances Industry Efforts to Address ADAS Calibration Complexity
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: CCC Intelligent Solutions Inc. (CCC), has announced Calibration Guidelines, a new capability that brings recommendations from leading providers directly into existing estimating workflows.
As advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) become more common and complex, repairers and insurers need trusted calibration guidance at the point of decision.

“The growing complexity of today’s vehicles is raising the stakes for every participant in the repair ecosystem,” said Dan Risley, vice president, Automotive Services Group for CCC. “Supporting safe, proper and consistent repairs requires collaboration across repairers, insurers, automakers, diagnostics providers and technology partners. CCC is helping make trusted calibration guidance easier to access and apply as repair and claims decisions are being made.”

Industry stakeholders, including leading repair associations and consumer advocacy groups, have increasingly identified ADAS calibrations as one of the collision repair industry’s most pressing issues, citing the need for easier access to trusted repair guidance.

“ADAS represents one of the most significant technological changes our industry has ever faced,” said Erick Bickett, director, PACE Calibration Centers. “The pace and magnitude of this change demand collaboration across the entire industry. We appreciate CCC’s leadership in making calibration guidance more accessible at the point where critical repair decisions are made and for their work as part of CIECA’s ADAS Calibration Committee. Together, these efforts are important steps toward greater transparency and proper repairers.”

articles.title: Volvo, Mercedes-Benz separately expand NVIDIA partnership for automated driving
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: Volvo and Mercedes-Benz have separately expanded their partnerships with NVIDIA to advance automated driving, according to press releases from both automakers.

The automakers will be provided with NVIDIA’s Hyperion in-vehicle computing and sensor architecture through the partnerships. They will also have access to NVIDIA’s Alpamayo Stack for full-stack driving software and AI reasoning capabilities.

Volvo says it will combine its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with NVIDIA’s technologies. It will enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door. This will include everything from highways and busy urban streets to parking scenarios.
The automaker will also use NVIDIA’s Halo operating system.

“Volvo has been synonymous with car safety for almost 100 years,” said Håkan Samuelsson, Volvo Cars president and CEO, in the release. “By working with NVIDIA, we bring together two distinct strengths: industry-leading safety knowledge and world-class AI technology. That combination gives us a unique opportunity to create safer and more attractive cars for our customers.”
Jensen Huang, NVIDIA founder and CEO, said that accelerated computing has transformed the car into an intelligent machine.

“Volvo has spent nearly a century protecting people on the road,” Huang said. “Together, we’re combining Volvo’s extraordinary vehicle safety systems with NVIDIA Hyperion and Halos to build a new generation of cars that make driving safer and more effortless.”
The automaker plans to debut the technology in a next-generation car.
Volvo and NVIDIA have been working together since 2017.
Mercedes-Benz says its partnership with NVIDIA brings together the automaker’s engineering and safety expertise with its MB.OS operating system.

The automaker’s operating system supports new driving functions and over-the-air updates, the release states. It adds that with NVIDIA’s technologies, the system can support point-to-point urban assistance, active safety, and automated parking.

NVIDIA’s Halos builds on the Mercedes-Benz safety foundation, including a parallel safety stack that adds redundancy and guardrails, the release adds. Together, the technologies support advanced driver assistance and the development of future SAE-Level 4 applications, including robolimousines.

“NVIDIA is our most important strategic partner in automated driving,” said Jörg Burzer, Mercedes Board of Management member and Development and Procurement chief technology officer, in the release. “Together, we developed the first Mercedes-Benz assistance system for urban point-to-point driving for the Western world. The expansion of our partnership marks a significant milestone and reflects the mutual trust we have built over the years. Together, we aim to bring further pioneering innovations to the road, offering our customers the best automated driving experience while upholding the high safety standards they expect from a Mercedes-Benz.”

articles.title: Insurer Report Card survey opens Nov. 1; why the results matter
articles.author: Lurah Lowery

paras.en: CRASH Network’s Insurer Report Card survey opens Nov. 1, and John Yoswick filled Repairer Driven News in on how the three-minute survey garners important information for the collision repair industry and consumers.

“The key reason that we believe shops should participate is the Insurer Report Card can then help educate consumers,” said Yoswick, CRASH Network’s editor. “We get 1,000 shops participating, and the result is a free report that anyone can download, including consumers, showing grades for 90-plus insurers.”
It asks collision repairers to grade each company from A+ to F based on how well the insurers’ claims practices help ensure quality repairs and customer service.

He added that the survey isn’t just on the top 10 national insurers; it includes smaller, regional carriers, depending on where carriers do business. Depending on where insurers do business, repairers oftentimes grade 20 or 30 carriers in their respective state.

“In past years, it’s often those smaller insurers that are among the companies receiving the highest grades from shops,” Yoswick said. “It’s a tool that shows consumers that they have more choices than they may realize and reminds them that there’s something other than just price to consider when they’re buying insurance.”
Other considerations include how insurers will handle their claim.

“That’s something shops see every day and can compare one insurer to another,” Yoswick said. “We also believe the more shops that are aware of the Insurer Report Card and that participate and use the report, the more consumers will be made aware of it. That’s our No. 1 goal — to help provide a tool for shops and consumers to use to show that there are differences among insurers.”

Around 1,100 shops typically respond to the survey each year. Yoswick said the more shops that participate, the more validity and credibility the Insurer Report Card gains. More participation also means more insurers for a consumer to learn about, he said.
Yoswick noted that insurer grades aren’t reported in the Insurer Report Card until a set minimum number of shops have graded that insurer.
“Even getting just a half dozen or 10 more shops participating in a state can add one, two, or three good insurers to the report for their particular state,” he said.
Insurers pay attention to the Insurer Report Card results and often ask for details on the “why” behind the grades they receive, Yoswick said.

“All that individual information remains strictly confidential, but when shops take the time to answer some of the follow-up questions in the survey about the insurers they graded, it helps us develop some cumulative data to show, for example, that some insurers get a low grade even from their DRP shops,” he said. “We can show that some companies get a lower grade primarily because they’re parts policies or just because their claims processes are more burdensome or just because shops see them as being less responsive than other insurers.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: He added that insurers who receive the best grades are increasingly using that in their marketing. Plus, other publications and organizations, including The Wall Street Journal, Money, and USA Today, incorporate Insurer Report Card findings into their own scoring system for auto insurers.

In addition to grading insurance companies specific to each survey respondent’s state, optional questions focus on parts policies, payment for OEM repair procedures, and delve deeper into insurer claims processes.
Yoswick says the Insurer Report Card findings are a tool for shops and trade associations to use when speaking with lawmakers or insurance regulators.

“I think a lawmaker or an insurance regulator might sometimes hear, ‘Well, all shops don’t like any insurers,’ and there’s a lot more nuance than that,” he said. “When shops are talking with regulators and lawmakers, they can use the Insurer Report Card report to show that there’s some insurers handling claims in better ways for consumers.”
He added that the Insurer Report Card includes regional data breakouts and state-specific reports when there are enough survey respondents.

According to the last Insurer Report Card, released in February, seven auto insurance companies received an A-minus or higher. Thirty-five insurers received a B or higher, earning an Honor Roll spot. Twenty-two carriers, including six of the largest U.S. auto insurers, received a C-minus or lower.
None of the top 10 largest national auto insurers received an overall grade higher than a C-plus, while more than 60 other insurers ranked higher.

Yoswick spoke about the survey at the Society of Collision Repair Specialists’ IDEAS Collide Showcase at the 2025 SEMA Show. He said thousands of consumers, insurance regulators, and insurance carriers download the report card results every year. The survey is currently in its 10th year.

articles.title: Copart completes ACV Auctions acquisition
articles.author: Lurah Lowery

paras.en: Copart completed its acquisition of ACV Auctions on Friday, according to a Copart press release.
ACV is a digital automotive marketplace and data services partner for dealers and commercial clients. Copart announced the $1.9 billion cash deal on Sept. 10.
ACV common stock shares have ceased trading on the New York Stock Exchange. ACV will now operate as an independent subsidiary of Copart led by ACV’s existing leadership team.

“We are pleased to complete the acquisition of ACV, which is an important milestone for Copart as we continue to deliver on our growth strategy,” said Jay Adair, Copart’s CEO, in the release. “With ACV now part of the Copart family, we have established an industry-leading, fully complete remarketing platform spanning dealer trade-ins, wholesale remarketing, salvage disposition, and international scale. Together we bring stronger capabilities, great efficiency, and an expansive footprint, and we’re excited about what we will be able to deliver for our customers moving forward.”

paras.en: Adair discussed the acquisition during the company’s Sept. 10 Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings call with investors.

“We are excited about using our locations as staging areas for their vehicles and combining our global buyer base with their digital marketplace and remarketing technology,” Adair said at the time. “Copart and ACV are highly complementary. We bring physical scale, deep institutional relationships, salvage expertise, and international buyer demand with more than 275 locations, over 4 million vehicles sold a year, and approximately 1 million members across more than 185 countries.

“ACV brings dealer liquidity, relationships, and inspections and valuation technology, transacting approximately $10 billion of gross merchandise value in 2025 across more than 22,000 active buyers. Copart completed the cash tender offer, through its wholly owned subsidiary Apple Merger Sub, Inc., to acquire all issued and outstanding shares of ACV common stock at a purchase price of $10.50 per share, net to the seller in cash, without interest, subject to any applicable withholding taxes.

As of the Oct. 15 tender offer expiration, 116,818,409 shares of ACV common stock were validly tendered (and not validly withdrawn), representing 68.43% of the total number of ACV’s issued and outstanding shares of common stock, according to the release. All shares have been accepted for payment.

“ACV’s mission is not complete, and we will continue to revolutionize the used vehicle sector,” said George Chamoun, ACV CEO, in the release. “Joining with Copart amplifies this mission, supercharging our growth, pace of innovation, and global reach. By combining forces and tapping into Copart’s massive national physical presence alongside a global buyer-seller network — we will unlock unprecedented value for our commercial and dealership partners, ensuring every vehicle finds its ideal buyer. I want to extend my heartfelt thanks to our exceptional ACV team, and we are thrilled to embark on this next chapter with the Copart team.”

His focus as CEO includes bringing members together through collaborative workshops where they can exchange best practices and learn from one another. articles.title: Turning ADAS Calibration into a Competitive Advantage
articles.author: Autel

paras.en: See how Zimbrick of Madison transformed its approach to ADAS calibration by bringing more of the process in-house. With three body shops, 16 automotive brands and a centralized glass and calibration center, Zimbrick partnered with National Calibration and Diagnostic Solutions (NCDS) and Autel to build a more controlled and scalable calibration workflow. The video explores how the right equipment, training and support can help collision repair facilities improve efficiency, documentation, repair quality and customer communication while keeping up with increasingly complex vehicle technology.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - Bringing ADAS calibration in-house: Zimbrick reduced its reliance on outside vendors to gain greater control over scanning, calibration and the overall repair process.
- Centralizing calibration services: A hub-and-spoke model allows three body shops to work with a centralized calibration center while maintaining consistent processes.
- Improving repair quality and accountability: In-house capabilities give Zimbrick greater visibility into technician training, OEM procedures, documentation and how calibrations are completed.
- Combining glass and calibration: Locating glass replacement and ADAS calibration together allows Zimbrick to complete more windshield installations and calibrations on the same day.
- Training the entire team: Education extends beyond technicians to estimators, helping staff better understand ADAS requirements and explain necessary procedures to customers.

- Building customer confidence: Employees can explain why a calibration is required, what equipment is being used and how the procedure fits into a complete repair rather than simply presenting an additional charge.

- Getting more from ADAS technology: Autel equipment provides diagnostic, calibration and documentation capabilities, while NCDS provides tooling recommendations, training, workflow guidance and ongoing technical support.

- Creating a scalable operation: With approximately 400 repair orders moving through the operation each month, bringing scans and calibrations under Zimbrick’s control helps turn a necessary repair procedure into an opportunity for greater efficiency and additional in-house service.

articles.title: Value Added: Creating a Culture Beyond Cost
articles.author: Thomas Dayton

paras.en: In case you haven’t noticed, the parts business is a pretty crowded marketplace. In my own little hometown of less than 30,000 people, we have EIGHT parts stores! There are also eight OEM dealer franchises, so there is certainly no lack of options for purchasing auto parts and supplies in our area… and that doesn’t even include online options. With 16 places offering parts in the immediate area, if we want to make a sale we have to make our offerings more attractive than everyone else.

In order to stand out in a crowded market, your operation needs to add value to your products beyond whatever your competitors are offering. That “value” may take the form of different things to different consumers, but this sort of “it factor” is integral to making you stand out in a crowd. Since there are so many kinds of added value, identifying those things your customers value can be challenging.

The Value Stick may sound like some off-brand deodorant, but it’s a concept endorsed by Harvard Business School to visualize the four factors that help build a value-based business strategy. At the top of the stick is a customer’s “willingness to purchase” (WTP), and at the bottom lies your own “willingness to sell” (WTS). In between the two are your cost and the selling price of a product. These four markers are all, to some degree, moveable up or down The Value Stick. WTS primarily concerns the vendors who supply your parts and employees who provide labor for your store. It is the lowest price at which you can purchase your stock and pay someone to sell and distribute it to your customers. WTP, on the other hand, depends solely on a customer’s estimation of your product’s value, and represents the maximum amount of money they will hand over for your product at the point of sale.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Price can be a funny thing. For some, a higher price signals an increase in quality over a less-expensive product (brand name vs. generics, for example), or the cache of luxury (they’d pay $50 more for a Tommy Hilfiger shirt than a similar garment from Wal-Mart). For others, a higher price only means your business is making excessive profits… at their expense. (“I can buy the same thing on Amazon for $20 less than your price, why are you so high?”)

I believe that many of our customers (professional and amateur alike) still view the products we sell daily as interchangeable commodities. As parts professionals, we know better, but when we are faced with those customers for whom “any old thing will do,” we have to use other means to attract them to spend their money with us. Of the four variables along the Value Stick, WTP is the one we have the most influence over. Short of renegotiating supplier prices or reducing staffing costs, we don’t have much control over the cost of our inputs. We must maintain a reasonable margin in order to pay our overhead and keep ourselves in business, so deeply discounting prices is not a long-term solution. The only remaining way to move the needle is to increase the value of our product. Not the individual gasket, chassis part, or alternator, but rather through the experience of purchasing it from us.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: All else being equal, people buy from the people and places they know and trust. It is easier to build these kinds of relationships with commercial customers simply because of the volume of their business. We have more opportunities to show them that we are an important partner in their success, and that we value that partnership. Prompt delivery, complete and accurate order fulfillment and ease of doing business are all value-added services that help justify a premium price tag. For the more occasional customer (professional or retail), we have a shorter window of opportunity to make a lasting impression. Superior customer service is still our greatest advantage with this sort of customer. Employing a knowledgeable and friendly staff, or even utilizing online lookup and ordering platforms can streamline the buying process for customers who value convenience.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Many retailers also build value into their product offering by providing additional services like code-reading, battery testing and installation, or loaner tool programs. Geared toward the non-professional segment of their customer base, these services also position the retailer as a trusted partner in maintaining personal vehicles. Adding value beyond the cost and quality of your parts increases retention and creates a scenario in which satisfied customers become advocates for your business. Give them something no one else can, and they have no reason to go anywhere else.

articles.title: Get Smart: Processes for Continuous Improvement
articles.author: Thomas Dayton

paras.en: Continuous improvement is a business strategy aimed at providing superior customer service through the implementation of a series of small changes in your operations and policies. These individual improvements may be centered around efficiency, productivity, employee happiness, or a multitude of other factors, but, ultimately, their purpose is to make your operation better at attracting, serving and retaining customers.

Continuous improvement is most closely associated with the Japanese word Kaizen. The post-World War II rebuilding of the Japanese industry led to several advances in manufacturing efficiency and quality control, many of which were the basis for “modern” manufacturing and business concepts like “lean” or “just-in-time” manufacturing, Six-Sigma quality control and improvement, and “The Toyota Way.” Each of these concepts has its own variation on identifying potential roadblocks to success, proposing solutions, implementing the means to those solutions, and analyzing the success or failure of any changes made.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Know your customer: by understanding the customer’s needs and wants, you can implement improvements that matter to them.
Let it flow: removing barriers to efficiency and reducing waste creates a smooth workflow.
Go to where the work happens: don’t manage from an office, see the problem firsthand.
Empower people: improvements and the resulting success require input from the “bottom up.”
Transparency: share plans, goals, and results with the entire team.

These principles can be applied to any problem in your operation, but continuous improvement is often used initially in smaller, incremental stages. These small changes are easier to implement, as they do not require a complete overhaul of company culture or the involvement of the entire staff. These can be “experimental” changes on a small scale, to test their effectiveness in specific situations or with a particular department. Breakthrough continuous improvements are larger in scale, and are most effective when a process or operation is in need of a complete overhaul. In either situation, proposed improvements should align with these five principles.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In order to transform the vague idea of a potential improvement into a clear plan of action with defined results, continuous improvement plans often rely on setting “SMART” goals. SMART is an acronym for “Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Timely.” SMART goals are a litmus test for determining if what you want to achieve is realistic and worthwhile to spend the time, energy, and money pursuing. Have you set a specific goal that accurately reflects the improvement(s) which you are hoping to implement? Can you measure the progress in a clear and meaningful way, so you know where you are in the process and know when you have achieved the goal? Is the improvement achievable with your current staff and resources? Are the changes relevant to your operation’s mission, values, and culture? And finally, is the goal time-sensitive? A goal without a deadline is more of a dream.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Once your organization has committed to continuous improvement and SMART goals have been set, the next step is to create and standardize the processes you want to use in working toward those goals. Staff must be given the tools (and the training) to implement any intended changes, and also an opportunity to express constructive opinions concerning the “real-world” effectiveness of the improvements. Project leaders should monitor the progress of each improvement project throughout the process and measure the results using key performance indicators (KPIs) tied to the results you hope to achieve through the planned changes.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: If the process yields positive results, you are (as an organization) one step closer to achieving your goal of serving your customers more effectively. Share your successes with those who helped create them, with others in the organization who may benefit from the discovery, and, most importantly, with the customers whom you are doing this for in the first place!

articles.title: Ultrasound waves that jiggle deep brain structures may relieve delusions in schizophrenia, small trial hints
articles.author: Lauren Schneider

paras.en: Stimulating the brain with ultrasound could help counter the delusions people experience in schizophrenia, a small trial finds.

The trial involved transcranial ultrasound stimulation, in which a device placed on a patient's head delivers ultrasound waves through the skull and into the brain. Its goal is to change the activity in a targeted brain region.

Delusions are false beliefs that are very difficult to shake; for example, a person might believe they are being stalked when they aren't or think that a major disaster is about to occur without any evidence to suggest so. In the trial, researchers found that a 10-minute session of the ultrasound treatment reduced the severity of delusions for at least a week in patients with schizophrenia or a related disorder.

This targeted ultrasound treatment delivered directly to the brain could avoid some of the full-body effects of antipsychotic medications, such as weight gain and high blood pressure. That said, the new results, published Tuesday (Oct. 20) in the journal npj Acoustics, are a first step and will need further verification in larger trials.

"It's too early to know for certain what the therapeutic benefits will be, but it's very exciting," study co-author Dr. Donald Goff, a professor of psychiatry at the New York University Grossman School of Medicine, told Live Science.

The pilot study included 10 patients with either schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder. In both conditions, patients experience psychotic symptoms, including delusions and hallucinations. Schizoaffective disorder also includes mood symptoms, such as mania.

The researchers interviewed each participant to characterize the content of their delusions, and also documented their cognitive state and experiences with auditory hallucinations — perceptions of sounds that aren't actually occurring. The participants then received both an ultrasound treatment and a placebo treatment, spaced one week apart.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

Other noninvasive therapies — such as transcranial magnetic stimulation, which uses magnetic fields — can also stimulate the brain. But the ultrasound technique differs from these therapies because ultrasound waves can penetrate deeper into the brain with greater specificity, study co-author Shy Shoham, a neural engineer at NYU Grossman, told Live Science. He compared the way a transducer directs ultrasound waves toward a given brain region with the way a lens focuses light.

In this case, the researchers focused this lens on a brain network called the cortico-striatal-pallido-thalamic circuit, which includes structures underneath the brain's outer cortex. The relationship between this circuit and schizophrenia symptoms is still somewhat unclear, partly because its deeper components are hard to study in adequate resolution with MRI, said co-author Dr. Wei Qi, a clinical assistant professor of psychiatry at NYU Grossman. However, some past studies have suggested that this network plays a part in schizophrenia.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Much of what scientists know about the network comes from research in movement disorders, such as Parkinson's disease, in which there is an imbalance between excitation and inhibition in the neurons that control movement. A similar dynamic could help to explain symptoms of schizophrenia, the scientists think.

"Our hypothesis is that, in schizophrenia, there is an imbalance between excitation and inhibition regarding what in the environment is actually important," Qi told Live Science. "The failure to inhibit irrelevant signals could be the basis of psychosis."

The researchers surveyed the study participants after each treatment, asking about the degree of belief each person had in their delusions and the amount of stress they caused. Compared with the placebo treatment, the ultrasound stimulation was associated with less-severe delusions over the following week. There was no significant change in patients' auditory hallucinations or overall cognition, though.

The ultrasound therapy came with mild side effects, such as fatigue and headache. Some patients had transient increases in delusions, which Qi attributed to normal fluctuations in symptoms that are expected in schizophrenia. These outcomes were just as common after the placebo treatment, so they may not be related to the ultrasound specifically.

The stimulation was aimed specifically at the right side of a brain structure called the globus pallidus internus (GPI). In a previous study, the authors found that greater connectivity between this region and another structure — the dorsal anterior cingulate gyrus — was linked to more-severe psychotic symptoms in schizophrenia. So, they made the GPI their target.

To date, "there haven't been many successful therapeutic attempts at targeting some of these deeper structures," said Dr. Deepak Sarpal, an associate professor of psychiatry at the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine who was not involved with the study. Ultrasound waves reach brain regions under the cortex in a less-invasive manner than deep brain stimulation, in which a surgeon implants an electrode in a patient's brain, Sarpal noted.

The researchers are not the only group using transcranial ultrasound to influence the cortico-striatal-pallido-thalamic circuit. Earlier this year, another group stimulated portions of the striatum, which is located directly under the cortex, in patients with schizophrenia. They evaluated hallucinations rather than delusions, finding that the treatment reduced symptoms for at least a week after the procedure.
In this line of research, the targeted nature of transcranial ultrasound presents advantages as a research tool as well as a treatment approach.

"If we find that a specific circuit or a node in a circuit seems to be closely linked to symptoms we're trying to treat, then it will be a matter of understanding what pattern of stimulation may allow us to correct that," Goff said. Qi, Goff and colleagues now plan to continue testing their technique on more patients and to experiment with different doses of ultrasound.
"A lot more work needs to be done," Goff said, "but we're really quite optimistic about its promise."

articles.title: Undeciphered Voynich manuscript may have been bound out of order, study finds
articles.author: Kristina Killgrove

paras.en: The mysterious and undeciphered Voynich manuscript has caused consternation among code-breakers, linguists and scholars of medieval literature for more than a century. But now experts think they've worked out why it's so hard to crack: It was bound incorrectly in the 15th century, meaning the pages are out of order. The new linguistic analysis of the document has moved researchers closer to figuring out what the text was all about.

The Voynich manuscript is a medieval codex made up of leaves of parchment carbon-dated to the early 15th century. Its 240 pages are covered with about 38,000 words of a unique script called "Voynichese" along with illustrations of people, plants and astrological symbols. Also known as the Beinecke Cipher manuscript, the document was initially owned by a Holy Roman emperor and was purchased by Wilhelm Voynich in 1912. Since 1969, the manuscript has been in the collection of Yale University's rare book library. Experts have unsuccessfully tried to decipher the manuscript for more than a century.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: "We don't know if it's a code," Lisa Fagin Davis, study co-author and executive director of the Medieval Academy of America, told Live Science. "But there are some odd characteristics of the Voynich manuscript in terms of its physical structure."

When doing research on the number of scribes who copied the document, Davis realized from the handwriting that the manuscript's pages alternate in ways that don't make sense. In addition, she said, "there are several examples where the image goes off the page in the middle and comes out on the other side, even though there are a bunch of pages in between."

In a study published Monday (Oct. 19) in the journal Digital Medievalist, Davis and co-author Colin Layfield, an information systems researcher at the University of Malta, suggested that the inconsistent structure of the enigmatic manuscript is the result of someone mis-binding a manuscript they were unable to read.

Medieval manuscripts were made up of rectangular sheets of parchment (animal skin), typically folded in half to produce what experts call a bifolium. Around five bifolia would typically be nested together, creating what experts call a quire. Then, a stack of quires would be bound together along the spine to create a book. However, Davis and Layfield suggested that the Voynich manuscript was intended to be a stack of singulions — a series of loose bifolia never meant to be bound together as a quire or a book.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: This is not the first time a researcher has suggested the Voynich manuscript has pages out of order. But Davis and Layfield analyzed the graphic properties of the untranslated document to see if their hypothesis made sense.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

"We're viewing it as a text and assuming it has a message," Layfield told Live Science, which means it should be possible to statistically compare blocks of text to see if they're similar or disconnected. Layfield used a technique called latent semantic analysis (LSA), which is a natural language processing technique invented in the 1980s to find hidden patterns in texts.

LSA is particularly useful for small sets of data, Layfield explained. "Modern AI techniques need ridiculous amounts of data to train on, which we just don't have. We've got just 35,000 or so words. That's it." The researchers' LSA analysis of the Voynich manuscript revealed that some pages had low similarity, suggesting they may not have gone together, while others had high similarity, bolstering the idea that they were supposed to be read together.
By looking at the Voynich manuscript as a collection of singulions, Davis and Layfield solved some of the nagging issues with the document.

"When you start to think about it in the context of the other strange features of the manuscript, all of those problems are resolved," Davis said. "It solves the problem of each scribe writing one sheet. It solves the problem of the images crossing the gutter."
This means that any previous work on the Voynich manuscript that assumes it was ordered correctly now needs to be reconsidered, she said, but it also means there is new progress on the book.

"This work helps us think about whether there's actual meaning underneath it all," Davis said. "It doesn't get us there," she said about a definitive translation, "but it moves the ball because you can't make sense out of a book where all the pages are mixed up."

Davis is optimistic that someone will crack the Voynich mystery, in part because a similar modern puzzle known as Cain's Jawbone has been successfully deciphered by a handful of people. This devilishly difficult linguistic puzzle from the 1930s consists of 100 pages of a murder mystery arranged in the wrong order. Due to the unique nature of the text and its vague, stylized language, even AI has failed to solve it.

"We have some ideas for other work we want to do," Davis said. For example, there's a large water stain in the upper margin of some of the pages of the Voynich manuscript. "The stain should be symmetrical from one page to the next but it's not. That also supports the idea that the manuscript is bound out of order."
Davis and Layfield are thinking about ways to compare the stain shapes across the pages, as that may help them reorder the incorrectly organized pages.

Kristina Killgrove is a staff writer at Live Science with a focus on archaeology and paleoanthropology news. Her articles have also appeared in venues such as Forbes, Smithsonian, and Mental Floss. Kristina holds a Ph.D. in biological anthropology and an M.A. in classical archaeology from the University of North Carolina, as well as a B.A. in Latin from the University of Virginia, and she was formerly a university professor and researcher. She has received awards from the Society for American Archaeology and the American Anthropological Association for her science writing.

articles.title: The James Webb telescope is watching one of the earliest supernovas in the universe unfold
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have found what may be one of the most distant supernovas ever observed. And in a stroke of cosmic luck, the team thinks they're seeing what the explosion looked like just days after it ignited.

The supernova, named AT 2026abck, dates to around 1.15 billion years after the Big Bang, when the universe was less than one-tenth of its current age and bursting with massive stars flickering into life. The massive exploding star violently released its light over 12.5 billion years ago, according to the researchers — so long ago that the distance between us has effectively ballooned sixfold due to the expansion of the universe.

The discovery was described in a paper that was uploaded to the preprint server arXiv Sept. 29 and has not yet been peer reviewed. According to the study authors, this ancient speck of light is stupendously bright.

"At its peak, the supernova is about 8 billion times the brightness of the sun … almost as bright as the whole Milky Way Galaxy," study co-author Xiaohui Fan, an observational cosmologist and professor of astronomy at the University of Arizona, told Live Science via email. "Over the course of the explosion, it radiates the energy that the sun will radiate over about 2 billion years."
A beacon from the beginning of space-time

The newly discovered supernova shines brilliantly at over 30,000 degrees Fahrenheit (16,000 degrees Celsius). Its incandescent shell of ejected material has billowed to a radius of approximately 46 astronomical units — about 46 times the distance between Earth and the sun, or about as far as Pluto swings at its farthest point from the sun.

The supernova's host galaxy, designated ID101411, holds about 6.3 billion solar masses and is "forming new stars more than ten times faster than our Milky Way," first author Mingyang Zhuang, an observational astrophysicist at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, told Live Science via email.

As with other early galaxies, ID101411 is deficient in metals, meaning any elements heavier than hydrogen and helium, because not enough time had passed to create those heavier elements in the forges of massive stars and their apocalyptic explosions.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

The study authors estimate that they observed the supernova as it would have looked just four to 10 days after it exploded. Although this is relatively common, spotting one at such an incredible distance "is extremely rare," Zhuang emphasized. "You have to observe the exact same tiny patch of sky repeatedly with [JWST], and the explosion has to happen at the right moment. We were lucky."

There's another layer of luck that made the discovery even more remarkable: It was observed without the aid of a cosmological quirk called gravitational lensing — a phenomenon predicted by Einstein in which the gravity of a massive object in space bends and magnifies the light emitted by objects behind it.

"Most supernovas this far away were found with help from a massive foreground galaxy cluster acting as a natural magnifying glass," Zhuang explained. "It's the most distant one we've actually seen appear."

This supernova was discovered as part of the NEXUS Treasury program, in which JWST intermittently scours patches of the sky for ancient explosions. It had previously observed the explosion's host galaxy over the past few years and finally witnessed the supernova on Aug. 7 of this year.

Intriguingly, the star had not yet exploded in JWST's previous viewing, on May 28, 2026, meaning that 71 days passed on our Earthly clocks, even though only about 12 days passed in the supernova's own time frame.
This highlights a mind-bending cosmological effect: The universe's expansion doesn't just stretch space; it slows down time from our perspective.

"Because the universe has expanded since this light was emitted, everything about this explosion appears to us in slow motion, about six times slower than it actually happened," Zhuang said. "Changes that took one week at the supernova take about six weeks to unfold from our point of view."
- Famous supernova that lit up skies in 1181 is now full of mysterious knots — Space photo of the week
- A star 20 times the size of the sun died in a supernova — and telescopes around the world joined forces to watch it
- Scientists mapped the shape of a supernova for the first time ever – and it's not what we expected: Space photo of the week
Mysteries still remain about the nature of this ancient explosion that shone so brilliantly we can observe it across nearly the entire universe.

Rather than a conventional core collapse supernova — in which a star between approximately eight and 50 times the mass of the sun exhaust its nuclear fuel and suffers a rapid core collapse and subsequent explosion — the recently discovered supernova may be one of the universe's rarest, most powerful explosions, the study authors said. Known as a superluminous supernova, this type of explosion releases tens or hundreds of times more energy than conventional supernovas. Whether the explosion continues to heat up or starts to cool could reveal exactly what is happening in its environment and what caused it, the team said.

paras.en: "Our interpretation is still preliminary," Zhuang concluded. "Follow-up observations will tell us more about exactly what kind of explosion this was."

articles.title: Archaeologists Searching for Evidence of a Norse Church in Greenland Have Found 'the Smoking Gun' Near Erik the Red's Settlement

paras.en: Archaeologists have discovered the remains of a Norse church in southern Greenland, a find that could offer new insights into the lives of the Vikings who once called the island home.

“Churches were vital in Norse society, which makes them key to understanding how their society, especially the power structures, developed,” Christian Edelfelt Koch Madsen, an archaeologist with the National Museum of Denmark and co-leader of the dig, says in a statement.

Norse settlers from Iceland, also referred to as Vikings, first settled in Greenland around 985 C.E., led by explorer Erik the Red. They lived on the massive island until the early 15th century, when they mysteriously vanished.

As Tim Folger wrote for Smithsonian magazine in 2017, Norse settlers didn’t “just get by” in Greenland. They “built manor houses and hundreds of farms; they imported stained glass; they raised sheep, goats and cattle; they traded furs, walrus-tusk ivory, live polar bears and other exotic arctic goods with Europe.” Such success, he adds, makes their disappearance all the more perplexing.

For decades, researchers have been conducting archaeological excavations in hopes of better understanding the rise and fall of Norse society in Greenland. In the early 2000s, researchers discovered a rectangular stone wall with the remains of a stone building in the middle, a layout that suggests the site was once home to Norse church. But to definitively confirm the building’s purpose, they wanted to find a cemetery.

In 2025, archaeologists once again revisited the site. On the final day of that excavation, researchers started unearthing bits of charcoal, which suggested humans had once occupied the site. Then, they found what appeared to be a decomposed human bone.

When researchers returned this past August, they uncovered the remains of an entire human skeleton buried with its arms placed by its sides and its head pointing east, a positioning that suggests a Norse Christian burial sometime during the early Middle Ages.

“This is ‘the smoking gun.’ Now there is no doubt that this is a church,” Madsen says in the statement. That would make it the first Norse church discovered in Greenland in more than 60 years. Based on its size and construction from hewn stones, the researchers suspect it dates between 1100 and 1300 C.E., a period that aligns with when Norse settlers in Greenland were transitioning to Christianity.

The church is located near the modern town of Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland, roughly three miles from Brattahlíð, the estate of Erik the Red and the primary hub for the entire Norse colony in Greenland, which numbered 3,000 individuals at its peak, Madsen tells the Viking Herald’s Jonathan Bennett.

In total, researchers have discovered the remains of six churches around Brattahlíð, likely constructed by rich local farmers or landlords. The researchers suspect they were competing for the religious power—and revenue—that accompanied church ownership. “These churches seem to demonstrate that, in the early Middle Ages, [Norse settlers] started competing about who’s going to run the show,” Madsen tells the Viking Herald.
- Born in Norway, Erik the Red left for Iceland after his father was exiled for manslaughter.
- During Erik’s own subsequent banishment from Iceland, the explorer first reached Greenland with a small group of men around 982 C.E. and returned three years later to start a settlement.
The site appears to correspond with a “Church Under the Sunny Mountains” mentioned in a medieval Icelandic manuscript called the Flateyjarbók, or the “Book of Flatey.”

The remains sit in front of a mountain range on the edge of the Greenland ice sheet, an area that often has sunny weather. However, as Madsen tells the Viking Herald, “there are a lot of mountains and a lot of places that look the same in Greenland.” The document mentions two other churches that could be nearby.

Looking ahead, the team plans to study the artifacts discovered during the recent dig. If they’re able to secure more funding, they hope to return to the church and narrow down when it was constructed.

In the meantime, they are still reveling in the success of the recent excavation, which “is another piece of the puzzle that may bring us closer to understanding what happened to the Norse colony in Greenland and the mystery of why it disappeared,” Konrad Smiarowski, an environmental archaeologist at the University Museum of Bergen and co-leader of the project, says in a statement, per High North News’ Trine Jonassen.
Editors’ note, October 20, 2026: A previous version of this article incorrectly stated the reason for the area’s sunny weather. The story has been edited to correct that fact.

articles.title: This Dog Learned to Sniff Out a Slimy Marine Invader Called 'Sea Vomit'—a Skill That Earned Her the Animal of the Year Award

paras.en: It takes more than a few tricks and a penchant for fetch to receive a prestigious animal award. A black Labrador from the Scottish Highlands just snagged one for her ability to sniff out “sea vomit,” a colloquial name for the carpet sea squirt, an invasive marine creature threatening the waters along Britain and Ireland, among other places.

On October 15, Sgiath (pronounced Skee-ah) was crowned Animal of the Year by the nonprofit International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW). The 6-year-old pooch and her handler, Texa Sim, a marine ecologist based near Glencoe, Scotland, were recognized for their pioneering work in marine conservation. According to IFAW, Sgiath is believed to be the first dog trained to sniff out carpet sea squirt—which, if left unchecked, can smother native species and colonize infrastructure like oyster farms and fisheries.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: “Every year, the Animal of the Year award celebrates animals doing extraordinary things, but Sgiath’s story is like nothing we’ve seen before,” says Sharon Livermore, director of marine conservation at IFAW, in a statement sent to media. “Her trailblazing work demonstrates the remarkable potential of dogs to contribute to conservation science in entirely new ways.”

Originally trained as a mountain rescue dog, Sgiath was later taught to recognize the scent of the invasive marine species. She has successfully sniffed out hundreds of colonies of the sea squirt, Kate Stephens and Victoria Gill report for BBC News. In fact, Sim tells the outlet that when Sgiath catches wind of a sea squirt colony, she’s never wrong—even when she’s sniffing through layers of seaweed on tricky structures, like pontoons and oyster cages.

“She’s a natural,” Sim says. Since first training Sgiath in marine detection, Sim has added to the sea squirt-sniffing team: a 3-year-old Labrador named Uisge, described as a “protégé” in the statement.

The carpet sea squirt first appeared in the United Kingdom in 2008. Scientists suspect the organism hopped aboard ships from its native Japan. The creature, formally called Didemnum vexillum, has already spread up the British coast, and conservationists are worried it will expand further. The sea squirt thrives in warmer waters, leading to increased concern as climate change continues to induce higher sea temperatures.

These and other invasive organisms can drain ecosystems of valuable nutrients, depriving endemic wildlife, Martyn Kurr, a marine biologist at Bangor University in Wales, tells BBC News. “These species also clog up aquaculture pens, marine infrastructure, and machinery such as boat propellers,” he says. In Europe, spotting and controlling these invasive populations costs millions of dollars each year.

But not touching them can prove disastrous: In 1969, an unchecked carpet sea squirt population nearly decimated a population of Portuguese oysters living off the coasts of Portugal and France, per Metro’s Sarah Hooper.

Carpet sea squirt colonies are hard to spot. They can be creamy white, tan, or even pale pink or orange, and they often cling to algae or seaweed, appearing like a layer of slime—or vomit. Traditional means of identification involve laboratory analysis and DNA testing, requiring valuable time and resources, Holly Evans reports for the Independent. Sgiath, on the other hand, needs just a nose.

Using dogs to sniff out invasive species is not a new practice. Conservationists have been putting pups to work on land for more than a century, Katherine Manwell reported for Midstory in 2024. The practice became more widespread only in recent decades.

“In the mid-’90s ... within the wildlife research community, there was a call for more noninvasive techniques for getting the same information that we [were] getting by trapping and radio-collaring all kinds of species and animals,” Alice Whitelaw, co-founder and director of programs at the U.S.-based nonprofit Working Dogs for Conservation, told the outlet.

While canines are not a catch-all, they tend to be more efficient and less invasive than other methods, per Midstory, allowing conservationists to identify and remove unwanted species without disrupting the environment.
However, Sgiath is unique: She’s not sniffing invasive critters on land; she’s hunting them at sea. The Labrador walks the beach, entering the water at low tide to sniff out any potential colonies.
“She just does a survey with her nose, essentially,” Sim tells BBC News. “She can pinpoint exactly where it is.”

Still, Sgiath and future sea squirt-sniffers in her mold cannot eradicate these colonies on their own. But “if we can identify the species earlier and more efficiently, it gives conservationists and site managers a much better chance of responding before the problem gets out of hand,” Sim says in the statement.

articles.title: The World's Tallest Trees Seem to Struggle to Make Their Own Food During Heat Waves, Leaving Them Vulnerable as the World Warms

paras.en: Coast redwoods are iconic giants of the Pacific Coast, found only in a narrow band of land stretching from central California to southern Oregon. These towering trees—the tallest in the world—are adapted to the region’s relatively cool, moist climate, particularly the thick summer fog that blankets their canopies during the dry season. But in recent years, the area has been getting hotter, and the fog has been dwindling, raising questions about how these ancient trees will fare in a warming world.

paras.en: Now, scientists say they have an answer. A study published September 22 in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences finds that coast redwoods slow photosynthesis when temperatures spike, a discovery that suggests climate change could be threatening the trees’ long-term health and survival.

Through photosynthesis, plants convert sunlight, water and carbon dioxide into oxygen and sugars, which provide the energy and building blocks they need to grow. As trees build trunks, branches, roots and leaves, they store some of that carbon in their tissues. Because of their large size, thick bark and long life spans, coast redwoods act as massive carbon sinks, keeping it out of the atmosphere for decades or even centuries.

To better understand how rising temperatures might be affecting these processes in coast redwoods, researchers studied trees growing in Garcia River Forest in Mendocino County, California, near the southern part of the species’ range. Once or twice a month from July 2022 through October 2024—a span that included two heat waves—they took measurements for individual leaves, colloquially called needles.

Their analyses revealed that, during bouts of extreme heat, the needles were up to 18 degrees Fahrenheit hotter than the surrounding air. “That’s a huge difference and indicates that the leaves are stressed to the point where they can’t thermoregulate effectively,” lead author Lily Klinek, an ecologist at the University of California, Davis, tells Live Science’s Sarah Wild.

Based on the temperature difference, the team suspects that the leaves’ stomata—small, pore-like openings that help release heat via water vapor—were at least partially closed to help the tree retain moisture. But stomata also play an important role in photosynthesis, taking in the carbon dioxide needed for the process, so the results also suggest that the higher temperatures could be hampering photosynthesis.
Did you know? The world’s tallest living tree

The world’s tallest living tree is a roughly 380-foot-tall coast redwood named Hyperion, located in California’s Redwood National Park. Discovered in 2006, Hyperion has been officially off-limits to visitors since 2022 because tourists kept veering off established trails and damaging the delicate forest ecosystem. The towering plant is estimated to be about 600 years old.

To measure the impact of heat on photosynthesis more directly, Klinek and colleagues collected samples from the lower canopies of younger coast redwoods, whose branches are easier to reach than those of massive old-growth trees. Back in the laboratory, the team submerged the leaves in water and exposed them to a range of temperatures between 72 degrees and 110 degrees. Though their stomata were open and they had access to all the necessary ingredients for photosynthesis, their photosynthesis rates declined as temperatures increased.

paras.en: This suggests that high temperatures might be directly affecting the trees’ ability to photosynthesize, rather than indirectly by prompting them to close their stomata and reduce their carbon dioxide uptake.

The findings indicate that coast redwoods are “really temperature sensitive,” Christopher Still, an ecophysiologist at Oregon State University who was not involved with the study, tells Science News’ Allie Skalnik. “You don’t see this as much with other species necessarily.”

Taken together, the study suggests that rising temperatures spurred by climate change could diminish coast redwoods’ ability to photosynthesize and store carbon. But it remains unclear whether the effects are temporary, or whether heat waves cause lasting damage. The researchers also say they haven’t discovered the point of no return—how hot it would have to get, and for how long, for that damage to become irreversible.

“Right now, the temperatures are coming back to normal in the fall and winter and letting the trees recover,” Klinek tells Vox’s Neel Dhanesha. “But in five or ten years, if temperatures are even hotter and heat waves are even more frequent, we don’t really know if there would be a recovery.”
